qs.whyOthersFail: The options “selama tiga belas menit”, “selama satu jam”, “selama sepuluh menit” are not supported by the text. What is written is “For thirty minutes we speak only English.”, and that matches the correct answer.

qs.stem: According to the text, what is true about Rosa?
options: She teaches Spanish at her school.
She comes to the club every day.
She has been studying here for one year.
She writes songs for the club.
qs.why: The answer is written directly in the text: “Rosa is studying at our school for one year.”. Therefore, the option is “Dia sedang belajar di sini selama satu tahun.”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The options “Dia mengajar bahasa Spanyol di sekolahnya.”, “Dia datang ke klubnya setiap hari.”, “Dia menulis lagu untuk klubnya.” are not supported by the text. What is written is “Rosa is studying at our school for one year.”, and that matches the correct answer.

qs.stem: What do the club members do after the English session?
options: They receive a small vocabulary book.
They go home at half past three.
qs.why: The text organizes events through “After that we speak Spanish with Rosa from Peru.”. Therefore, the answer is “Mereka berbahasa Spanyol bersama Rosa.”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The options “Mereka menyanyikan dua lagu berbahasa Inggris.”, “Mereka menerima buku kata kecil.”, “Mereka pulang jam setengah empat.” are not supported by the text. What is written is “After that we speak Spanish with Rosa from Peru.”, and that matches the correct answer.

qs.why: The text follows the relocation of the reading room upstairs and how the club and its new schedule operate.
qs.whyOthersFail: There is no reading competition, the desk was not bought with club money, and borrowing is served every break without restrictions.

qs.why: Angkanya jelas: empat ratus peminjaman bulan lalu, kira-kira dua kali total Januari.
qs.whyOthersFail: Two hundred is actually an approximate January figure, and what is being counted is borrowing, not the number of readers or a comparison of comics.

qs.why: In that sentence, “manage” means the club members run the borrowing desk themselves during every break.
qs.whyOthersFail: “Manage” can indeed mean to survive with difficulty or to handle money, but the sentence does not mention noise, payments, or book organization.

qs.why: Discussion is allowed after two o'clock and the morning must be quiet, so the hours are divided between quiet study and chatting.
qs.whyOthersFail: The quiet corner idea actually failed and was replaced by a schedule; the room opens at seven, and group revisions remain inside the library.

qs.why: The text mentions the club made posters for “recent arrivals” and then placed them near the canteen, so this claim is a direct paraphrase.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” does not work because no part of the claim is reversed; “Not stated” is ruled out because the poster is clearly written.

qs.why: The report follows Rani's class paper collection project for three weeks from the beginning to its follow-up plans.
qs.whyOthersFail: The garden is only a side source of income, the shop buys once rather than starting a habit, and exams do not stop the project.

qs.why: Uangnya dipakai buat enam tempat sampah kuat plus satu set alat berkebun.
qs.whyOthersFail: The paper box was from the teacher from the start, the chilies were planted not bought, and no exam papers were spent.

qs.why: Because the storage room fills up quickly, the classes agreed to move the collection day earlier.
qs.whyOthersFail: The hall was never used to pile up paper, the shop does not pick up every Friday, and the ones transporting the boxes remain two students.

qs.why: The reason is in the “because” clause: the class had to prepare for exams, so the box task was passed to younger ones.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kepala sekolah cuma memuji proyeknya, nggak ada perbandingan jumlah kertas antar kelas, dan Rani nggak bilang mau pindah ke kebun.

qs.why: The one paying for the paper is a small shop near the school, so the claim about a company in the capital city directly contradicts this.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because the buyer is different; “Not stated” is also wrong because the text mentions who pays.

qs.why: Seluruh isi emailnya jam muat van, jam kedatangan Sri, pakaian, dan makan siang, semuanya pengaturan hari pindahan.
qs.whyOthersFail: The van was already rented by Dimas's family, the new address was sent by his mother via message, and the busy week was only mentioned in passing without an apology.

qs.why: They plan to load the rented van at six in the morning, before the roads get hot.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jam tujuh itu waktu Sri diminta datang, sementara tengah hari dipakai makan siang dan sore Sabtu nggak pernah disebut.

qs.why: Dimas wrote labels on every box using a thick marker; his mother was the one who wrapped the plates.
qs.whyOthersFail: Plates are wrapped by his mother, the new van is loaded on Saturday morning, and the kitchen rack is already empty.

qs.why: The stairs are dusty, so the advice to wear old clothes is to keep good clothes from getting dirty.
qs.whyOthersFail: The van seats, the narrow new yard, and the refrigerator are indeed mentioned, but the only reason written is the dusty stairs.

qs.why: The van is mentioned, but the text never mentions any costs; the closest sentence is just about a new address note.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” requires numbers that are not in the text; “False” is also ruled out because there are no other rates written.

qs.why: From the four o'clock boat, changing prices, to dirty water issues, all are morning routines of the fish market.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ice is only used by sellers without a delivery story, the cook is not depicted as competing, and what the market office installed is a pipe, not a new building.

qs.why: Perahu sampai di pantai jam empat, lalu pekerja langsung mendorong kotak ke meja.
qs.whyOthersFail: Half past five is when the street is full of buyers, midday is the limit of ice preserving the fish, and the street is swept after closing.

qs.why: Last year the market office installed wider pipes near the gate for melted ice water.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ice is still used by sellers, the drain is easily clogged rather than closed, and the table is never moved.

qs.why: Prices go up and down every morning, which is why buyers still walk around asking several sellers first to find the cheapest one.
qs.whyOthersFail: The biggest fish is wanted by the restaurant cook, and the text does not say buyers come before the boat or check ice stock.

qs.why: The text says that when the sea is rough, fewer boats go out to sea and the price of a kilo of fish can double, which matches the claim.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” does not fit because the price trend is the same; “Not stated” does not fit either, because the relationship between weather and price is clearly written.

qs.whyOthersFail: Bagas is still captain and actually speaks in that report, the preparation comes after the loss rather than before, and the match is not replayed.

qs.whyOthersFail: Three quick goals actually came after the break, and Tuesday was only used for watching footage.

qs.why: He counted eleven moments when the goalkeeper's front area was left empty, so that defensive aspect is what needs fixing.
qs.whyOthersFail: Scoring in the first half went well, the ball was lost due to passes that were too slow, and footage was watched once, not every match.

qs.why: Kapten justru mengaku pemain mengabaikan peringatan pelatih di babak kedua, jadi klaim ini kebalikannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” conflicts with the word “ignored”; “Not stated” is wrong because the text does discuss that warning.

qs.why: The announcement is about a new bus route for students from villages east of the river along with its rules.
qs.whyOthersFail: The fee is only mentioned by amount without any increase, the parking lot already exists and is used for going home, and class hours do not change.

qs.whyOthersFail: The school gate is the morning destination, the parking lot is used when going home, and downtown is the old route.

qs.why: Students who have already received transportation assistance do not need to pay anything.
qs.whyOthersFail: Living east of the river, registering before Friday, or taking the old route does not make the fee disappear.

qs.why: The text says the return bus departs from the school parking lot at four o'clock, so this claim is just rewording.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” requires reversed content even though the location is the same; “Not stated” is ruled out because the return point is written.

qs.why: The sky gets dark quickly in the rainy season, so bright clothes make riders more visible.

qs.why: Hujan jatuh langsung ke meja di bawah atap bocor, jadi dua tetangga itu pindah ke luar biar dagangannya aman.

qs.why: They actually offered to cover half the cost, so the claim about refusing to pay directly contradicts this.

qs.whyOthersFail: “False” requires a reversal that is not there; “Not stated” is ruled out because that scene is clearly written.

qs.why: Audience members must buy tickets for five thousand rupiahs, so the claim about free admission contradicts the text.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is wrong because there is a ticket price; "Not stated" is also wrong because the price is clearly written.

qs.why: The canteen does not provide cold water in the late afternoon, which is why students look for drinks outside the gate.

qs.why: The text only says the survey covered three hundred students; who joined or whether all classes were represented is never mentioned.

qs.why: The announcement is about the schedule of two subjects swapping places, while the others remain the same.
qs.whyOthersFail: Exam week is not extended or postponed, and there are no new subjects; the roof work is just the reason.

qs.why: The math exam moves from Tuesday morning to Thursday afternoon.

qs.why: Pekerjaan atap masih berlanjut tiga hari lagi dan suaranya bisa mengganggu ujian, jadi jadwalnya digeser.

qs.why: The library is open until five every evening during exam week, so this claim is the same content in other words.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" requires reversed content, whereas the hours match; "Not stated" is ruled out because the opening hours are written.

qs.why: The article is about a narrow yard that can still produce vegetables, complete with methods and cost savings.
qs.whyOthersFail: The rented house is just background not a matter of price, the garage only provides cans without processing them, and the text talks about savings not the increase in chili prices.

qs.why: The cans are free because the garage at the corner of the street gives them away.
qs.whyOthersFail: The one at the corner is a garage not a shop, and what is exchanged with neighbors is young seeds, not cans.

qs.why: The holes are made at the bottom of the container so that water flows out and the roots do not die.

qs.why: Sunlight determines the arrangement, so the boards are shifted so that each plant gets light according to its needs.
qs.whyOthersFail: The children water twice a day without any connection to boards, the weight of the cans is not mentioned, and what is lent to neighbors are seeds, not boards.

qs.why: The text says chili plants need at least five hours of direct light, whereas those that tolerate shady spots are leafy vegetables.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" swaps the subject with leafy plants; "Not stated" is wrong because the chili plants' light requirements are written.

qs.why: Wisnu wrote because his grey bag was left behind under a chair and he wants the bag to be looked for.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dia nggak memesan kursi, nggak menuntut uang tiket, dan busnya memang langsung jalan tanpa dia menyalahkan sopir.

qs.why: He can come at noon or any afternoon except Wednesday, and that indeed means almost all afternoons.

qs.why: Nadia mencuci mangkuk, memotong kubis, dan mengisi kuali besar.
qs.whyOthersFail: The one tasting the broth is her grandmother, and Nadia's notebook contains changes she tried, not recipes or order lists.

qs.why: Within a week the queue reaches the fish section and the soup runs out before ten o'clock.
qs.whyOthersFail: Neneknya justru menolak menaikkan harga, sepupunya cuma menyarankan, dan keluarganya tetap di pasar lama.

qs.why: The long queue could be a reason to raise prices, but she still refuses, indicating her regular buyers matter more to her than profit.
qs.whyOthersFail: She actually refuses her cousin's suggestion, and the text does not mention a second stall or the writer's hope to return.

qs.why: The text only tells of the writer dropping by once by chance; whether she came again is never hinted at.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" requires a second visit that is not written; "False" also does not work because the text does not say she never returned.

qs.why: The article is about how a row of night stalls operates: peak hours, ways to attract buyers, and shared rules.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tea prices are never written, the bell is just one vendor's trick, and office workers are just markers of opening time.

qs.why: Jam tersibuk datang antara tujuh dan delapan, terutama di akhir bulan.

qs.why: A woman rings a small bell every time her batch of cakes is cooked.

qs.why: The fire is kept small because burnt food makes people stay away.
qs.whyOthersFail: The text does not mention firewood prices or lamp heat, and the one-meter distance is a street rule, not about fire.

qs.why: Those who ignore the sweeping rule actually lose their spot for two weeks, so this claim is the reverse of the rule.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" clashes with the written punishment; "Not stated" is wrong because the penalty clearly exists.

qs.why: The report is about a running club growing from nine to thirty-four members plus its new habits.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jalur rusak cuma satu masalah dan klubnya tetap jalan, nggak ada lomba antar sekolah, dan pelatihnya masih memimpin.

qs.why: Members gather at half-past five in the morning, before the sun gets too hot.

qs.why: Three members suffered ankle injuries on the rocky path, so the route was changed because it was dangerous.
qs.whyOthersFail: The bridge was not closed, the town square was chosen because it was safer not closer, and the parents did not request a long route.

qs.why: A parent rode a motorcycle behind the last runner for safety, the content is the same as the claim.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" requires the content to be reversed, even though the position is the same; "Not stated" is ruled out because the escort is written.

qs.why: Residents must place bags outside the gate before six o'clock.

qs.why: Kitchen waste must actually go into regular bags, not blue bins, so this claim is contradictory.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is wrong because the places were swapped; "Not stated" is wrong because the rules are written in full.

qs.why: The article compares a small station ten years ago with now: trains, platforms, and facilities have increased.

qs.why: The announcement is now read in two languages, so the claim about more than one language is true.

qs.whyOthersFail: The August performance happened long after she invited friends. The table went into storage at the end of the story. The new teacher was hired by the school, not Sari, and that was the very end.

qs.why: They chose a place that couldn't be heard so their mistakes wouldn't be watched by people.
qs.whyOthersFail: The table only went into storage at the end of the story, so it's not the cause. The ceremony happened in August, not during practice. The new teacher wasn't there yet when they were practicing.

qs.why: The text says the sound was rough and some started getting too fast, so the claim of “perfect” is contradictory.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because the quality was actually described as rough; “Not stated” is not appropriate because the performance was evaluated in that sentence.

qs.why: Pemesanan dibenerin dulu, terus dua hal penting diingetin.
qs.whyOthersFail: The narrow road is indeed mentioned, but the order was forwarded, not cancelled. The harvest festival is mentioned, and there is no request to change the date. The back room is offered, but the price per night is never mentioned.

qs.why: They park next to the mosque and then walk the last two hundred meters.
qs.whyOthersFail: The text says wide cars cannot reach the gate. The inner courtyard is used for breakfast, not parking. The village square is only mentioned as the direction the upper rooms face.

qs.why: “Carry your luggage” artinya bawain barang, asal jam datangnya dikabarin.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pick-up at the village square was never promised. Wide cars cannot go up to the gate. Breakfast is prepared by the inn, not the driver's duty.

qs.why: The back room is indeed quieter, but the text mentions those rooms do not have a valley view.
qs.whyOthersFail: A private bathroom is specified for the booked room, and there is no mention of a back room missing. Breakfast on the patio applies to all guests. Driver assistance with luggage also does not depend on the room location.

qs.why: The text only mentions two rooms booked; the total number of rooms in the inn is never stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” requires a total number in the text, which is absent; “False” is also incorrect because the text does not mention any other quantity.

qs.why: The content is about choosing a quieter time to arrive.
qs.whyOthersFail: The guide's habits, the closing schedule of distant rooms, and online ticket prices are all supporting details. The main point of the article is choosing a quieter visiting hour.

qs.why: Cafes and shops inside might not be open yet, so hot drinks must wait.
qs.whyOthersFail: The text states that the morning light in the showroom is actually fresh. Morning staff even have time for questions. Temporary exhibitions are also still empty in the first hour.

qs.why: The furthest room closes first, so go there first.
qs.whyOthersFail: The text suggests buying tickets online, not at the counter. Asking the guard is never suggested; the closing time of the distant room is already written. The temporary exhibition is mentioned for morning visitors.

qs.why: The queue at the counter is longer, while the price is the same, so buying online saves more time.
qs.whyOthersFail: The text explicitly states the price is the same, not cheaper. The counter closing time is never mentioned. Tour groups arrive during peak hours, and their bookings are not discussed.

qs.why: “Plan their visits around it” means they schedule their visits to avoid peak hours.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” is incorrect because no part is reversed; “Not stated” is wrong because the guide's habits are written.

qs.why: Laporannya nyeritain kunjungan, hasil hitungan, dan dua masalahnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Mangrove roots are discussed, but park admission fees are not. The tide table and forgotten boots are indeed the issues, not the main point of the report. The invitation to return is mentioned, but plans to stay longer are not.

qs.why: “Waterproof cards” are water-resistant cards where they write down numbers.
qs.whyOthersFail: A park map was never made. Numbers were not read out to the staff, but recorded. The cards are kept by the park, not the school office.

qs.why: The number nine is for the driest box; thirty-one is for the wettest.
qs.whyOthersFail: Thirty-one is the wettest box, so it is the reverse. Ten is the number of students per group. Two is the side length of the inner box in meters, not the number of trees.

qs.why: The tide came in faster than the printing schedule, so the table needs to be verified earlier.
qs.whyOthersFail: The forgotten boots are a separate issue, unrelated to the tide table. Park staff did not ask for a new plan. The bus leaves at four, as planned.

qs.why: The bus returns at four, not six in the evening; the numbers were swapped.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because the times are different; “Not stated” is incorrect because the return time is written.

qs.why: The text acknowledges the benefits of recycling songs but warns of the dangers, which is why a balanced approach is recommended.
qs.whyOthersFail: The audience is relaxed, but winning a competition is never written. Honest feedback is given by the teacher, and it is not mentioned to be recorded by the students. Minor keys change the weight of the lyrics, but class preference is not discussed.

qs.why: The audience becomes more relaxed as soon as they recognize the song.
qs.whyOthersFail: The text does not say the audience monitors arrangement changes. The original singer is indeed brought to mind, but that is a long-term risk, not an immediate reaction when the song is recognized. Singing along is also never mentioned.

qs.why: Rearranging the arrangement teaches song structure more deeply than theory lessons.
qs.whyOthersFail: Choosing a pitch for the voice is not mentioned as the lesson. Honest feedback comes from the teacher after the performance. Audience preference is discussed in the first paragraph, not as a result of rearranging the song.

qs.why: Kalau cuma main aman, penyanyinya nggak pernah punya suara sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Forgetting the lyrics of the original song is never mentioned. The audience stopping their attendance is also not in the text; what is mentioned is the audience remembering the original singer. The teacher is specifically said to give feedback after each performance.

qs.why: The text states that the words gain different weight once shifted to a minor key.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” cannot be used because no part is reversed; “Not stated” is wrong because the effect is written in that sentence.

qs.why: Isinya ajakan buat ikut nanam pagi-pagi di hari Minggu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Monthly checks are just the duty of three volunteers after planting. Registration at the gate and distributing gloves are implementation methods, not the main call to action.

qs.why: There are sharp clam shells in the mud, so feet must be covered.
qs.whyOthersFail: Wet morning soil is natural to imagine, but the text does not mention it. Boots are never discussed by the office. Storm surges are a threat to trees planted too close to the water, not the reason for covered shoes.

qs.why: Kantor nyediain sarung tangan dan makan siang sederhana; air dibawa sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Drinking water and long pants are actually brought by the volunteers themselves. Closed-toe shoes are also the volunteers' responsibility. Signs on the ground are made by forest rangers, not items distributed.

qs.why: The text mentions that trees planted too close to the water were washed away in the first storm.
qs.whyOthersFail: No staff member moved the trees to drier ground. Faster growth is also never mentioned. Monthly checks did exist, but that was a volunteer task for all trees, not a result of planting too close to the water.

qs.why: The text only mentions the plan to plant them; the reason why they were planted is never explained.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” requires a written cause which is absent; “False” also cannot be used because the text does not mention other causes.

qs.why: The writer wrote “I believe the school is wasting a decent idea by refusing to organize it properly”, so their push is for the school to reorganize the timetable.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable suggestions for any school, but the text rules out all of them: “The failure is not the pupils' fault” means the task is not shifted onto the students; the writer wants the leaflet replaced (“Replace the leaflet with a brief practical session”) rather than handed out earlier; and “would demand very little money and no additional staff” rules out asking the council for additional staff funding.

qs.why: The supporting detail is survey data: nearly three quarters of the 210 students asked to meet people who have just entered the working world, which is precisely the content of the session proposed by the writer.
qs.whyOthersFail: The extra leaflet was only requested by 19 out of 210 students, so it was not a majority request. The figure of 19 refers to the leaflet, not to moving the session to Friday morning; the schedule change was never surveyed. And the head of year admitted the plan was designed “for teachers, not for the people sitting in the room”, which is the exact opposite of the last option.

qs.why: Pengakuan “the current plan was designed for teachers, not for the people sitting in the room” langsung nyatain rencananya dibikin buat guru, jadi itu dukungan paling tepat.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three actually appear in the text and sound like evidence, but they do not address the claim: “no member of staff appears responsible” shows no one was in charge, not that the session was designed for teachers; “instructed to read it at home” merely shows the session was superficial; and “only 19 requested additional leaflets” measures student preference, not who the plan was designed for.

qs.why: The writer states “If the school attempted this for one term, I am confident that attendance would rise on its own”, and what they proposed is a session that answers real questions.
qs.whyOthersFail: All of these are sensible ways to increase attendance, but the text rules out three of them: the leaflet is meant to be replaced, not improved (“Replace the leaflet”); “would rise on its own” explicitly rejects the need for coercion or tracking attendance; and the proposal is to “Invite three former pupils each month”, not alumni every week.

qs.why: The text mentions that only 19 out of 210 students requested additional leaflets, so “a small number” is a paraphrase of that same figure.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” does not work because the text does not reverse the numbers; “Not stated” is also wrong because the figure is written explicitly.

qs.why: Tiga syarat penutup laporan (“a frequent service, clear signs, and a review after one year”) bikin intinya: lajur bus ngurangin keterlambatan asal busnya sering.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable interpretations for a traffic study, but the text rules them out one by one: the road is actually “one crowded road”, so it is not a quiet road free of cars; “car journeys grew longer by only two minutes” rejects the idea that delays were shifted to cars; and clear signs are only one of three conditions, whereas “Where no bus operates every few minutes, a reserved lane simply stands empty” makes bus frequency the deciding factor.

qs.why: The text notes that the average bus journey time dropped from 31 minutes to 22 minutes after the lane was created.
qs.whyOthersFail: Thirty-one minutes is the figure before the lane was opened, not after; and twenty-eight and nineteen minutes do not appear in the report; the decrease is from 31 to 22 minutes.

qs.why: Cars only added two minutes while buses dropped from 31 to 22 minutes, resulting in a small loss for cars and a nine-minute saving for buses.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are plausible outcome patterns for a bus lane, but the text's figures are different: “fell from 31 minutes to 22” creates a bus time saving of nine minutes, not four; and “car journeys grew longer by only two minutes” shows cars actually took more time, rather than saving nine minutes or staying the same as before.

qs.why: The evidence in the text points to a single conclusion: car travel times only increased by two minutes “because fewer people were driving”, and the researchers concluded that the delays feared by drivers “was largely caused by their own numbers, not by the missing lane”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are plausible accusations in any city, but the text rules out all of them. The phrase “not by the missing lane” rejects the removed lane as the cause. Signs only appear as a condition for success (“clear signs”), not as something ignored by drivers. And buses actually get their own lane, so stopping in mixed traffic was never measured.

qs.why: The text states that roughly one in nine former drivers switched to the bus, so the claim that “most” did reverses the numbers.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is incorrect because one-ninth is far from a majority; "Not stated" cannot be used because the transfer figures are in the text.

qs.why: The text says "What separates them is the kind of cost you are willing to accept", then each paragraph points out which buyer fits which route.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable intentions for a shopping article, but the text blocks them: "Both routes now include a guarantee" makes the guarantee unable to be a differentiator between buyers or proof that both routes are equal; and the seller is only mentioned once ("emphasize whichever margin favours them"), not as the article's target.

qs.why: The text mentions the battery may have lost one-fifth of its original capacity.
qs.whyOthersFail: There is no sentence about the battery being replaced before being resold; its power is also described as diminished, so it is impossible for it to be more durable than a new battery; and the guarantee in the text applies to both routes without excluding the battery part.

qs.why: Harga ponsel baru disebut “roughly double the amount a two-year-old repaired handset costs”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable price differences in the phone market, but the text's figures are different: "roughly double" is much larger than one-fifth, and "a fifth" in the text refers to the lost battery capacity; the comparison is also with two-year-old used handsets, not with the price of that model two years ago; and if the prices were the same, the entire cost paragraph would make no sense.

qs.why: The closing sentence mentions "The honest question is not which phone is better, but how long you intend to keep it".
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are benchmarks actually used by buyers, but the text places them below the duration of use: price is only a comparison ("roughly double"), camera and messages are just examples for one type of buyer ("mainly want a camera and messages"), and five years of updates is mentioned as a return on investment "If you intend to keep a phone until it dies", so the duration of use remains the deciding factor.

qs.why: The text only mentions both routes now come with a guarantee, without ever stating how long the guarantee lasts, so the two-year figure cannot be confirmed from the text.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is incorrect because the guarantee duration is never written; "False" is also incorrect because the text does not state the guarantee is shorter or longer; it is silent on the duration.

qs.why: Resensinya nyimpulin “Where the app genuinely wins is in the small print” sambil ngakui fiturnya “competent rather than brilliant”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors are claims that actually appear in the second paragraph of this review, but each is a side detail, not the main assessment. Device storage and a single rented server are merely technical details in the middle of a feature list. The annual report on official requests and exports limited to two forms are two correct details but not considerations weighed by this review. Search box speed is included in the section rated "competent rather than brilliant". The emphasis is stated by the author: "Where the app genuinely wins is in the small print" versus "the design feels plain beside its commercial rivals". The last option is indeed a summary, but it is misdirected: speed is actually rated "competent rather than brilliant", while the small print is what is praised.

qs.why: When first opened, the app displays a single screen listing every permission it will ever request.
qs.whyOthersFail: Rented servers abroad and annual reports do exist, but both are discussed later, not on the first screen; note storage location is also not displayed when first opened; what appears is a single screen containing all permissions that will be requested.

qs.why: Pujian buat “small print” nunjuk notis privasinya sendiri: “extends to 600 words and is entirely free of the usual fog”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are actually in the text and equally show the app is open, but it is not about the written terms: permissions not requested and "a single screen listing every permission" are app behaviors, and the annual report on official requests is company practice; only the 600-word notice talks about the small print.

qs.why: The text mentions "there is no drawing tool at all" and advises "if you need shared editing or handwriting, look elsewhere".
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable solutions for users, but the text blocks them: exports are only "plain text and a single archive", so they do not accommodate images; the plain design is called a weakness ("feels plain beside its commercial rivals"), not a help for drawing; and there is no promise that a drawing tool will come; one rating is even withheld because that tool is missing.

qs.why: "abroad" in the text has the same meaning as "outside the country", and the text clearly mentions copies of notes are stored on that rented server.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is incorrect because no proposition is reversed; "Not stated" is incorrect because storage on an external server is mentioned directly.

qs.why: The letter offers "Two lanes from eight until nine would enable our junior squad to train", so what is requested is an earlier time for the junior squad.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable requests from a club, but the letter blocks them: the club states "willing to transfer one session to weekend mornings and to pay the usual lane fee", so the fee is not requested to be waived and only one session is moved; and "the remaining lanes remain available to the public" rejects asking for all lanes.

qs.why: Average attendance dropped from 31 swimmers to 17, so roughly half of the previous figure.
qs.whyOthersFail: Thirty-one is the figure before the change, not after; the decline is not only among adult members because eight junior members quit; and the drop from 31 to 17 is much deeper than one-fifth.

qs.why: The sentence "Parents state plainly that they refuse to collect a twelve-year-old at that hour" points out exactly why the new slot closes the door for children.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are in the letter and sound supportive, but they do not touch on the children: the figure "from thirty-one swimmers to seventeen" counts all members, not just juniors; the assessment "unsustainable for a junior programme" is the coach's opinion without mentioning the cause; and eleven years of training only shows the club is old, not that children are locked out.

qs.why: The proposal "Two lanes from eight until nine ... while the remaining lanes remain available to the public" shows the club is looking for a safe path for both parties.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are attitudes that usually appear in schedule dispute letters, but the text blocks them: the club writes "We would prefer to propose a compromise rather than a complaint" and asks to meet, so they are not waiting for a rejection; the complaint is specific to juniors ("closing the club to children"), not adult members; and there is not a single sentence about moving pools.

qs.why: Nine-thirty is the start time plus half an hour, whereas the text mentions training only finishes at ten-thirty.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is incorrect because the time is shifted by one hour; "Not stated" is incorrect because the training end time is written explicitly.

qs.why: The author closes their argument with the analogy "complaining about empty lanes resembles blaming an unfinished bridge for the river", so the lanes that look empty only indicate the network is not yet connected.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors are real claims from other paragraphs of this column, but none are the main argument. The fivefold figure is the answer from the supporting side quoted by the author to show both camps have figures. Lanes that stop at a roundabout appear as a concession, "None of this makes every lane sensible". The neighbors' fear is supporting evidence from the author's experience. The emphasis is on "Until then, complaining about empty lanes resembles blaming an unfinished bridge for the river". The first option is also a summary, but the capacity figure is brought by the author as an answer from the supporting side, not as the foundation of their own argument.

qs.why: The supporting figure used by the author: protected lanes carry up to five times more people per hour compared to car queues, so that road space is not for "a handful of riders".
qs.whyOthersFail: The bike count at eight in the morning is the method of the opponents, and the text never says that count is rising; what is mentioned as rising for twenty years is the length of time the road has been unsafe. The lane between parked cars and buses is called "worse than nothing", so it is not a supporter. And the reason neighbors stay in cars is "fear rather than comfort".

qs.why: The text says "Both sides can quote figures, yet only one of them has to explain why parents refuse to let their children ride", so the burden is not balanced just on the issue of fear.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three sound reasonable for arguing with figures, but the text blocks them: the counting time is only used to blame opponents, not to praise the honesty of supporters; "Both sides can quote figures" rejects the idea that only one party uses figures; and the text never mentions who is included in the count, it mentions cyclists only appeared after the lanes existed.

qs.why: The lane that stops at a busy roundabout is called "worse than nothing", so cyclists can be worse off than before the lane existed.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable assessments for a half-finished lane, but the phrase "is worse than nothing" closes them all: if it is worse than nothing, it cannot be called helpful to the confident nor suitable for short trips; and the author attributes the arrival of cyclists to a network without "a single frightening gap", not to a lane that ends at a roundabout.

qs.why: The text mentions the reason neighbors stay in cars is fear, not comfort, so this claim is a direct paraphrase.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is incorrect because the reason is not reversed; "Not stated" is incorrect because that reason is written explicitly.

qs.why: Laporan nyebut rantainya lugas: “from the timetable to the sleep, and from the sleep to the following day”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors are actually stated in this report, but each is one link or one note of caution, not the main point. Body temperature and excitement are explanations for why sleep decreased, not the findings. The 47-minute difference is one measurement within that chain. The warning that the figures should not be transferred elsewhere is a limitation of scope. The emphasis is stated by the author: "The chain therefore runs from the timetable to the sleep, and from the sleep to the following day".

qs.why: Groups that train later sleep 47 minutes less, so slightly under fifty minutes.
qs.whyOthersFail: More than an hour exceeds the text's figure; one-tenth of a night is the magnitude of the test score decline, not the amount of sleep lost; and half an hour is the time needed for players to calm down after hard training; the sleep loss was 47 minutes.

qs.why: Morning reaction and memory test scores dropped by about one-tenth and muscle soreness lasted a day longer; those are consequences carried over to the following day.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are original findings of this study, but none talk about the following day: 47 minutes is the measure of lost sleep, not the consequence; "kept the players alert for roughly half an hour" explains the cause of the sleep loss; and the consistency of the effect direction between two squads talks about the reliability of the figures, not the morning impact.

qs.why: Peneliti nekenin “They observed one academy, one season, and one age group, so the figures should not be transferred elsewhere without checking”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three sound like standard scientific caution, but the text is different: researchers did not predict the effect weakens in older players, they only said one age group was observed; "should not be transferred elsewhere without checking" exactly reverses the option that figures can be used in other clubs; and "the direction of the effect was consistent across both squads" rejects the claim the effect was only in one squad.

qs.why: The text measures sleep, body temperature, reaction, memory, and muscle soreness; appetite or hunger is never measured in this report.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is incorrect because the data is not in the text; "False" is incorrect because the text also does not state the opposite, it is just silent.

qs.why: The text closes its comparison with "The correct choice depends on how certain you already are".
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable conclusions from the comparison of two routes, but the text blocks them: "The risk of regret is genuine on both sides" rejects the claim that apprentices automatically choose better; more doors is only one side of the scale; and wages per field are mentioned only to show the picture is mixed ("the two groups end up close"), while the benchmark used by the author is the reader's level of certainty.

qs.why: After ten years, engineering and health graduates tend to have higher wages, while in software and construction both groups are close, so the result depends on the field.
qs.whyOthersFail: Apprentices are not described as superior in all fields; wage similarity only applies to the two fields mentioned, not all; and health graduates are actually an example whose wages rise, not fall.

qs.why: The text mentions a degree in a broad field "leaves several doors open", whereas an apprenticeship trains one skill deeply and "may be harder to leave at twenty-eight".
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable ways to talk about career flexibility, but the text blocks them: wages from the first month are mentioned as a monetary advantage, not flexibility, and the skill path is actually "harder to leave"; the two paths are also not described as equal regarding doors; and "may be harder" only mentions it is more difficult, not that it closes off changing paths at age twenty-eight.

qs.why: The text says "If your interests are still moving, paying for time to explore is not weakness but sense".
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are pieces of advice usually given to school graduates, but the text blocks them: choosing one skill quickly is required "If you know the work you want", so it is not for those who are still hesitant; the benchmark used by the author is not which is cheapest but how certain you are; and there is not a single sentence about delaying both paths for a year.

qs.why: The text mentions apprentices finish without debt, so the claim about leaving training while bearing debt is a direct opposite.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is incorrect because it contradicts the text; "Not stated" is incorrect because the apprentice's debt position is mentioned clearly.

qs.why: Kolomnya nyebut “The saving in time belongs to me alone” sementara bahan bakar, kemacetan, dan tekanan ke kurir ditanggung seluruh distrik.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors are real claims from other paragraphs of this column, but each is supporting, not the argument. Comparing six items with two hundred items is evidence for the cost claim. Buyer choice for slower boxes is part of the medicine section, not the thesis. The app that chooses without asking is an opening anecdote. The emphasis is on "The bill is paid by other people" and "The saving in time belongs to me alone". The last option is also a summary, but the app that chooses first is only an opening anecdote; this column closes with who bears the costs.

qs.why: List of shared costs in the text: half-empty vans, drivers tied to schedules, and packaging "chosen for speed rather than weight", three things paid for by other people, not the buyer.
qs.whyOthersFail: Protection of fragile items and waste reduction at depots are never mentioned as reasons for packaging selection. The weight of slow shipping packaging is also never compared; what is mentioned is only that fast packaging is chosen for speed, not for weight.

qs.why: Paket dua jam bisa jalan di van berisi enam barang sementara paket tiga hari jalan bareng dua ratus barang.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable comparisons between fast shipping and slow shipping, but the text blocks them: the figure of two hundred belongs to three-day packages, not two-hour packages; package weight is never compared, what is compared is the number of items per van; and "The additional fuel, the additional traffic" shows there is an additional cost, not zero.

qs.why: The proposal consists of precisely three things: make the slow option the default, clearly display the price difference at checkout, and “offer a modest credit to customers who wait”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are sensible store policies, but the text rules them out: what is offered is “a modest credit to customers who wait”, not an extra fee for those who want speed; the requested default is the slow option, not the fast option; and “Speed should be something we request” shows the fast option still exists, just not assigned automatically.

qs.why: “the majority of buyers” has the same meaning as “most customers”, and the text notes they chose the slower box without protesting.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” is wrong because no proposition is reversed; “Not stated” is wrong because the retailer's experiment results are mentioned directly.

qs.why: The emerging pattern is described as having “had less to do with features than with revenue”, so this report explains what actually lies behind the requests for contact lists.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable topics for a privacy report, but the text rules them out: the features are described as “invented afterwards to justify it”, so the report did not compile a list of features that genuinely needed contacts; how ad partners store data was never examined (“They did not inspect the code”); and the app store was only asked to write reasons next to the button, rather than being depicted as checking permissions.

qs.why: The text mentions that 92 companies responded, which is slightly under one hundred out of the 200 contacted.
qs.whyOthersFail: Two-thirds is the proportion of apps requesting contact lists; nine out of ten is how often ad partners are mentioned in the notice; and a quarter is the proportion of apps actually using contacts for visible features.

qs.why: Where that request appears, ad partners are mentioned in the notice nine out of ten times, showing a direct link between the request and money.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are actual numbers from the study, but none of them connect the request to money: two-thirds only measures how common the request is; a quarter using it for visible features shows the request is often unnecessary, rather than explaining the reason; and 92 responding firms is a measure of the methodology, not a finding.

qs.why: The chain is complete in the text: two-thirds of apps request contact lists, only a quarter use them for something users are aware of, and developers' explanations culminate in “the feature is invented afterwards to justify it”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The text provides figures that refute each distractor. “Only a quarter used it for anything a user would notice” refutes the idea that the feature is noticed by most users. The order mentioned in the text is the reverse of the third option: requests come first, features follow. And what makes ad partners pay more is “A network of contacts”, not the features.

qs.why: Out of 200 apps examined, only 92 firms replied, so the claim that “all of the firms” did contradicts the figures in the text.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because the number of replies is well below the total; “Not stated” is wrong because the number of respondents is written explicitly.

qs.why: The rating of “three marks out of five” is the result of weighing factors: very useful for daily commuters with new phones, fragile for occasional passengers and older phones.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors are recorded in this review, but each is a single gain or loss, not the overall verdict. Automatic weekly rates are one of the advantages. Failure to open underground is one example of uneven reliability. Elderly passengers returning to paper tickets is a noted consequence, then used in the closing sentence as a condition for the fourth grade. The verdict itself reads "it is both better and worse than the system it removed", with a daily versus occasional sorting. The last option is a verdict, but only weighs one side; this review states "it is both better and worse than the system it removed".

qs.why: Twice in three weeks the app refused to open underground, a place with no signal.
qs.whyOthersFail: The app is not just slow or losing offline tickets, and clearly not running normally: twice in three weeks it refused to open underground because there was no signal.

qs.why: Elderly passengers at the author's stop “quietly returned to purchasing paper from the driver”, so the paper system is still more suitable for them.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable conclusions about elderly passengers and new technology, but the text blocks them: they actually returned to paper, so the app is not yet more suitable and has not replaced paper at that stop; and the author wants paper retained “for the passengers who depend on them”, so the two systems are not equal for them.

qs.why: The author says the app deserves a four “if the office retained paper tickets for the passengers who depend on them”, so the removal of paper removes a reliable option.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable consequences of removing paper tickets, but the text blocks them: purchasing on the app is called “eleven seconds instead of a queue”, so queues are not what is returning; the weekly limit is only mentioned as an automatic benefit, not something to be changed; and the office actually intends “to end in June”, not to bring back paper next year.

qs.why: The text mentions automatic fares calculated at a cheaper weekly rate, so this claim is just a paraphrase of that feature.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” is wrong because nothing is reversed; “Not stated” is wrong because the weekly fare feature is clearly mentioned.

qs.why: Penulis minta “the decision that this counts as literacy”, yaitu privasi masuk jadwal pelajaran resmi.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable positions in the digital education debate, but the text blocks them: “pretending it belongs to parents alone has ceased to be honest” rejects handing it over to the home; “Pupils are not careless” rejects accusations against students; and “Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher” rejects demands for new equipment.

qs.why: The Year Ten survey reinforces the main idea: students have vocabulary for old threats (viruses) but do not have words for things they hand over every day, so the gap is indeed in the curriculum.
qs.whyOthersFail: The second option reverses the survey results. Requests for password lessons were never surveyed; passwords only appeared in the table of contents of the six proposed lessons. And the text actually says assuming this matter belongs to parents “has ceased to be honest”, not that parents have explained it.

qs.why: The sentence “Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher” exactly shows the proposal does not add costs.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are actually in the text and sound supportive, but do not talk about costs: the assumption of employers and universities shows why the lesson is needed; the ability to name viruses measures student knowledge; and the list of letters, graphs, and swimming only shows what is already taught in school.

qs.why: The text mentions “Pupils are not careless; they simply possess no vocabulary for the thing being taken”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable explanations about teenagers and app permissions, but the text blocks them: “Pupils are not careless” rejects accusations of carelessness and there is no comparison between levels; warnings from home are never mentioned as existing, instead families are said to be unable to be left alone with this matter; and if they understood the exchange, the sentence about the lack of vocabulary would not make sense.

qs.why: The text only proposes six new lessons and mentions schools have not taught anything about it yet; the amount that “has already been taught” is never detailed.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because that number is not in the text; “False” is wrong because the text does not state the opposite specifically, it is just silent on those details.

qs.why: A three-year study of 1,200 students concluded “the answer depends almost entirely on the number of hours”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors are factual statements from other paragraphs of this report, but each is one side of the findings or one suggestion, not the central finding. The more organized eight-hour group is half the pattern. Surrendering revision time and rest is the mechanism, "The cause was not the employment itself but what it replaced". The suggestion that schools ask earlier is a recommendation. The central finding reads "the answer depends almost entirely on the number of hours".

qs.why: Above twelve hours the pattern reverses sharply: grades drop, absenteeism rises, and sleep decreases by almost an hour on work nights.
qs.whyOthersFail: Their grades dropped, not rose; the praise for neatness is for the group under eight hours; and family reports are never cited in the text.

qs.why: The text mentions the heaviest hour group “surrendered revision and rest first, because those were the only parts of the week nobody was paying for”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable causes for falling grades, but the text blocks them: night shifts before exams are just report advice for employers, not findings; “The cause was not the employment itself but what it replaced” rejects work fatigue as a cause; and there is no data saying that group was already behind before working.

qs.why: Some long-hour students “were supporting families and had no choice”, while the monetary value they received was not measured, so the study figures did not capture their situation.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable guesses regarding students who work out of necessity, but the text blocks them: the report does not predict hours will decrease next year; this group's scores are not separated from other long-hour groups, so one cannot say the decrease is smaller; and school assistance is never mentioned; what is mentioned is “the study did not measure the value of the money they earned”.

qs.why: The text mentions the study ran for three years, from Year Ten to the end of Year Twelve, so the one-year claim reverses the duration.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because the duration is three years; “Not stated” is wrong because the year range is written explicitly.

qs.why: Nasihat jujurnya “to choose according to the obstacle rather than the ambition”, jadi patokannya hambatan di bulan keempat.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable benchmarks for choosing an exercise method, but the text blocks them: the phrase “rather than the ambition” explicitly rejects ambition as a benchmark; price is only a determinant if your goal is routine (“the cheaper option is usually the stronger one”), not a general rule; and January and October are just markers of habit endurance, not a basis for selection.

qs.why: The text mentions that gyms require a monthly fee and a commute, and it is at that commute point that memberships usually die silently.
qs.whyOthersFail: Actually, it is the gym that has instructors to correct form; the condition of the machines is never complained about; and bad weather is mentioned as irrelevant indoors, that is a problem for running in the park.

qs.why: The text says “Strength is easier to build indoors, whereas the habit itself is easier to build outdoors, because the barrier is lower on a tired evening”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable win-loss divisions between the gym and the park, but that sentence blocks them all: strength is actually the strong point indoors, so not the park; the gym wins on strength but loses on habit, so not both; and “the barrier is lower” on a tired evening applies to running in the park, not to the gym.

qs.why: The text mentions that “you need supervision after an injury, the fee purchases something real”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable advice for someone recovering, but the phrase “the fee purchases something real” blocks them all: the fee is actually said to purchase something real, not to be a waste; the park's advantage in the text is about habit, not safety after injury; and the habit-first sequence is intended for people who want to be routine in October, not for people who need supervision.

qs.why: The text mentions that running in the park is almost free and provides no instructions, so this claim paraphrases two identical features.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” is wrong because no proposition is reversed; “Not stated” is wrong because cost and instructions are directly mentioned.

qs.why: The author states that their house “has never purchased such items in your shops” and wants to know how the offer was selected for them.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable requests from an upset customer, but the letter blocks them: the three requests are just data copies, a list of receiving companies, and permission to store the card without grouping, rather than an order to stop sharing data; product prices are never questioned; and they demand an explanation for their own case, not a rewrite of terms for all customers.

qs.why: Staff on the phone said the offers were compiled from similar households, a phrase that actually does not appear in the card conditions.
qs.whyOthersFail: Store managers are never mentioned as offer selectors; nine years is the author's duration as a customer, not an eligibility requirement for the offer; and the staff explanation speaks of household groups, not a single household record.

qs.why: Syarat kartu cuma nyebut catatan pembelian dipakai buat memperbaiki pengalaman belanja, dan “That wording does not reveal whether the records are shared with other firms”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three actually appear in the letter and sound supportive, but do not touch the vagueness of the conditions: the baby product discount offer is the event that triggered the letter; the card issue date is just background; and the fourteen-day reply deadline is a procedural rule, not proof that the conditions are silent on data sharing.

qs.why: The sentence “A vague sentence about experience is not consent” shows their view: general phrases cannot be counted as true permission.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are sensible attitudes towards terms and conditions, but the letter blocks them: the staff phrase is called “appears nowhere in those conditions”, so the phone explanation does not close the gap; address grouping “should have been declared plainly at the moment I signed” even though no data came out; and “a legal obligation rather than a courtesy” completely reverses the option regarding courtesy.

qs.why: Penulis justru minta tetap bisa pegang kartunya sambil nolak pengelompokan, jadi klaim soal minta kartunya dibatalkan itu kebalikannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because the letter does not ask for cancellation; “Not stated” is wrong because the desire to remain a customer is written explicitly.

qs.why: Usulannya persis: “Replace the grade with a record of participation, personal progress, and one skill of the pupil's own choosing”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are sensible grading reforms, but the text blocks them: the author only talks about sports marks and even mentions “Maths does not lose you friends in the playground”, so it is not all subjects; they want their marks replaced, not kept secret; and rewards for effort are actually the defenders' argument for grades, not their proposal.

qs.why: Pembela nilai bilang tanpa nilai, pelajaran olahraga bakal dianggap jam istirahat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Rewards for fast students were never a concern of theirs; what they mention instead is rewards for student effort that will never be fast; teachers' attitudes on planning are not discussed; and July is the month marks are released, not the month students stop attending.

qs.why: The text mentions “Maths does not lose you friends in the playground, whereas a low mark for running certainly can”, plus “how public the performance is”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are sensible comparisons between sports and academic subjects, but the text blocks them: the sentence about the playground actually says mathematics does not make you lose friends, so the last option's direction is reversed; recovery from bad marks is never compared; and grading strictness is not discussed, what is discussed is how public the performance is.

qs.why: The text states that if “the aim of school sport is an adult who still moves at forty”, measuring speed at fifteen becomes irrelevant.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are sensible goals for school sports, but the text blocks them: “measuring speed at fifteen is beside the point” rejects the search for the fastest student; exam grading is kept only “for those who take sport as an examination subject”, not for all students; and marks are what the author wants replaced with reports.

qs.why: The text mentions that grading is kept for those who take sport as an examination subject, so this claim is a direct paraphrase.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” is wrong because the exception is indeed written; “Not stated” is wrong because the sentence is in the final paragraph.

qs.why: Only “the manner in which the cost was printed on the label” was changed, and shopping patterns still shifted.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable consequences of the label experiment, but the text blocks them: the experiment mentions “the same products, the same prices, the same positions”, so store prices and bestselling shelves did not change; and shopping duration was never measured; what was measured was basket contents, including the baskets of hurried shoppers.

qs.why: In the second period, the price per hundred grams appeared beside the package price in the same font size.
qs.whyOthersFail: No warnings of any kind were attached to the labels; prices at other stores were never printed; and shelf positions were precisely left exactly the same on purpose.

qs.why: Sales of the cheapest option per gram rose by 14 percent, so people could actually compare without calculating in the aisle.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three actually appear in the report and sound supportive, but do not show that a comparison took place: eleven weeks in one chain is a methodological measure; differing label rules across regions are used by researchers to blame no one; and the chain that had already started changing is background, not a result.

qs.why: The text states that if clear labels divert money to better value, “the current design is not an accident but a choice”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are sensible readings regarding label design, but the text blocks them: the phrase “not an accident but a choice” directly rejects the accident option; regional rules are only mentioned as the researchers' reason to withhold accusations, not the source of the design; and “Shoppers had not suddenly grown wiser” shows the problem is not shopper habits.

qs.why: The text only mentions sales shifts between products, not total store revenue; overall profit-and-loss figures are never reported.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because total revenue is not in the text; “False” is wrong because the text also does not state the opposite, it is simply silent.

qs.why: A mark of three out of five is described as “weighted almost entirely by one week”, namely the application week which was considered truly useful.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors actually appear in this review, but each is a detailed complaint, not the core verdict. The interview week content is an example of a thin section. The mentor turning out to be a monthly call is an added complaint. Certificates with no recognition value are a closing remark. The core verdict is stated as "three marks out of five, weighted almost entirely by one week" along with "chiefly for the application week".

qs.why: The third week makes you produce four real documents, get comments from a human reviewer within two days, and then rewrite them.
qs.whyOthersFail: Videos, quizzes, and free questionnaires are the thin content of the interview week; and the monthly call for ninety participants is the form of the promised “mentor”, not the content of the third week.

qs.why: Pekan wawancara cuma berisi “two videos, a quiz, and a list of questions available free elsewhere”, jadi isinya nyaris bisa dicari sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable comparisons between course weeks, but the text blocks them: the interview week is called “remarkably thin”, so it is not the one with the most practice; human reviewer comments only exist in the third week; and “Nothing in the programme addresses salary, contracts” rules out options about pay and contracts.

qs.why: The promised mentor “proved to be a monthly group call with ninety participants”, far from personal guidance.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are sensible guesses about online course mentors, but the text blocks them: the two-day reply comes from “a human reviewer” in the third week, not from the mentor; no extra monthly fees are mentioned; and “The strongest section is the third week”, so the mentor is not the strongest part.

qs.why: “without charge” in the text has the same meaning as “at no cost”, and the text mentions half the material just repeats what the school provides for free.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” is wrong because nothing is reversed; “Not stated” is wrong because the repetition of school material is mentioned directly.

qs.why: The text mentions “The genuine difference sits behind the window, in what each company requires from you in order to survive”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable goals for an email service comparison article, but the text blocks them: “Neither answer suits everybody” rejects designating one best service for business matters; password recovery is just one detail of the free service's advantages; and the sentence about the difference behind the window rejects the conclusion that both are nearly the same.

qs.why: The free service notice allows message scanning to compile interest groups, because the email itself is the product.
qs.whyOthersFail: Storage is actually described as generous because the email is the product, so it is not deleted once the limit is reached; hiding messages from advertising partners is a promise of the paid service; and copying to a second company is never mentioned in the text.

qs.why: Layanan berbayar disebut “fewer tools, weaker protection against junk mail, and a real risk that the company closes”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable balances for paid services, but that sentence blocks them all: fewer tools and weaker protection reject both the winning and equivalent options; and generous storage actually belongs to the free service (“its storage is generous”), while message scanning is what the paid service promises not to do.

qs.why: The closing sentence says “A service you never chose is still a service you are paying for, in one currency or another”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable conclusions from this comparison, but the text blocks them: the free service is paid for with message scanning, so it is not without cost; for recipients of receipts and friends' messages, “paying to hide them from an advertiser may not be worth the expense”, so the paid one is not always the cheapest; and habit is mentioned as what usually decides, whereas “What matters is deciding deliberately”.

qs.why: The text mentions the free service actually wins on password recovery, so this claim reverses the direction of the comparison.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because the direction is opposite to the text; “Not stated” is wrong because the password recovery issue is discussed explicitly.

qs.why: The text mentions “An unpaid position does not select the strongest candidate; it selects the candidate who can afford to be unpaid”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors are real claims from other paragraphs in this column, but each is a step in a chain or a piece of evidence, not the argument. The three-month cost in a big city is the first link. Minimum wage experience is a proposed solution, not the thesis. The employer's report about brilliant interns is part of why they wrongly conclude merit. The argument lies in "An unpaid position does not select the strongest candidate; it selects the candidate who can afford to be unpaid".

qs.why: This cost detail is what connects the chain of argument: if three months of rent, transport, and food exceed many families' income, the applicants who can afford to stay are those with spare rooms or parents sending money.
qs.whyOthersFail: The wages saved by the employer are never calculated in the text. A month of transport costs is far from the figure mentioned, which combines rent, transport, and food for three months. And there is no reimbursement at the end of the summer; the position is indeed unpaid.

qs.why: Where minimum wage is mandated, “the number of positions fell slightly and the range of applicants widened sharply”, a trade-off the author considers worthwhile.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are indeed in this column, but none defend the pay: the same family appears repeatedly and the rent-transport-food cost is a description of the problem; and the employer's honest report about intern quality is actually part of the circle being criticized.

qs.why: Employers report “honestly enough” that their interns are good and then recruit from that group, so they think the narrow selection is fair.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable guesses about employers, but the text blocks them: the phrase “honestly enough” rejects the accusation of intentionally misleading; “they recruit from that group” rejects the option of recruiting from outside; and “convinced that they chose on merit” shows they are actually unaware of who is being excluded.

qs.why: The closing sentence explicitly asks organizations that cannot afford to pay to ask if they really need interns, so this claim is a direct paraphrase.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” is wrong because the advice is not reversed; “Not stated” is wrong because the invitation is written explicitly in the third paragraph.

qs.why: Laporan nyimpulin “The problem therefore sat at the edges of the journey rather than inside the vehicle”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors are indeed reported in this study, but each is a partial finding or an experimental result, not the main point. Nine minutes of walking without lights is only one of two points of rejection; the second is waiting at a remote stop. The crime rate remaining low is a comparison, not a conclusion. The one-third increase on one route is a trial described as "encouraging rather than conclusive". The main point reads "The problem therefore sat at the edges of the journey rather than inside the vehicle".

qs.why: The walk from the stop to the front door averages nine minutes and passes through unlit ground in most districts.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ten minutes, four minutes, and fourteen minutes are not in the report; the walk from the stop to the front door averages nine minutes.

qs.why: “Reported offences along the routes remained low, and the passengers already using them felt entirely secure”, so the fear is not a result of crime figures.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are original findings of this report, but none rule out crime as the cause: nine out of ten who are anxious only measure how widespread the fear is; nine minutes of walking without lights shows where the fear arises; and the one-third increase in female passengers is the result of an improvement trial.

qs.why: The three proposals are street lighting, accurate arrival schedules, and permission to alight between stops; the text closes that list with “None of these measures demands a fresh route or an additional vehicle”, in line with “remedies of remarkably modest expense”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Frasa “remarkably modest expense” nolak simpulan bahwa biayanya di luar jangkauan kota. Petugas di pemberhentian terpencil nggak pernah masuk tiga usulan itu. Dan “or an additional vehicle” persis nutup opsi tambah kendaraan.

qs.why: The text only mentions nine out of ten people interviewed feel the same anxiety; those waiting in pairs and those waiting alone are never separated into two groups.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is wrong because the comparison between passengers in pairs and passengers alone has no data in the text; “False” is also wrong because the text does not state that the pair group feels differently; on that matter, it is silent.

qs.why: Keluhan utamanya soal aplikasi: “It sends four notifications a day, sets targets I never chose, and converts a missed walk into a broken record”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable complaints for a fitness band, but the text blocks them: “Purchase the band for its honest numbers” shows the numbers are actually the part being praised; the complaint is not a lack of guidance but excessive encouragement; and the hidden three menus are “the switch that silences it”, not its best feature.

qs.why: Pulse during running is stable and close to a chest monitor, but deviates significantly when the effort changes suddenly.
qs.whyOthersFail: The two percent difference is about step counting; the match with the chest monitor applies during stable running, but actually deviates when the effort changes suddenly; and the strongest part of this device is not its pulse.

qs.why: Two nights of poor sleep are actually given high scores while one comfortable night is reported as interrupted sleep.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are indeed in the review, but none are about sleep scores: step counting and the waterproof strap are actually parts praised as a device, and the pulse deviation is a weakness in measuring sudden effort, not proof that the sleep score is wrong.

qs.why: The text says “Anyone who already worries about exercise will find that pressure unhelpful”, and the off-switch is hard to find.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable suggestions for people anxious about exercise, but the text blocks them: the numbers are actually recommended (“Purchase the band for its honest numbers”); four notifications a day are the source of that pressure, not its benefit; and the chest monitor is only used as a benchmark for accuracy, not as a purchase recommendation.

qs.why: The text mentions the price is equivalent to a good pair of running shoes, so the claim “far less” reverses the price comparison.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is incorrect because the price is equivalent, not much cheaper; “Not stated” is incorrect because that price comparison exists in the first sentence.

qs.why: The letter states “We should like to suggest two possible changes, either of which would assist”, namely leaving five minutes earlier or stopping at the corner.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable requests from the parents' committee, but the letter blocks them: the chaotic attendance list is mentioned as the result, and what is requested is a schedule improvement; “We are grateful for the additional service” shows the additional service is not what was requested; and class times were never proposed to be shifted; what is discussed is the bus departure and its stop points.

qs.why: The schedule puts the bus at the gate at 7:41, while six weeks of observation show an average arrival of 7:52, which is eleven minutes late.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nine minutes before class is a plan on paper, not reality; five minutes earlier is a proposed change in departure; and exact punctuality is refuted by the 7:52 average.

qs.why: The sentence “the office spends its first hour correcting the register” shows that the lateness drags the school into being affected.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are indeed in the letter, but they do not show the school bearing the burden: 7:41 is a plan on paper; eleven past eight measures how bad the lateness is; and two intersections that hold up traffic explain the cause on the road.

qs.why: Surat nyebut “The drivers are not at fault; the timetable simply does not match the street”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable causes for lateness, but the letter blocks them: “The drivers are not at fault” rejects accusations toward the drivers' departure; there is not a single sentence about students missing the bus; and what changed at the start of the term was the bus schedule, not the class time.

qs.why: “supply the full record” has the same meaning as offering to share the data, so this claim is a paraphrase of the letter's closing sentence.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” is incorrect because the offer is not reversed; “Not stated” is incorrect because the willingness to share records is written explicitly.

qs.why: The text mentions “Neither option is universally superior” because “the two journeys suit different distances and different streets”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable conclusions for a comparison between roads, but the text blocks them: walking safety is acknowledged as true but “neither settles the question”; cycling only pays its costs “where a safe route exists”, not for most families; and the benchmark mentioned is “The sensible test is the map rather than the principle”, not the child's fitness.

qs.why: Walking is said to require no equipment, keys, or repairs of any kind, and a nine-year-old can do it alone in most neighborhoods.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keys and dry storage are the price of cycling; quiet sidewalks are actually the best condition for walking, not something to be avoided; and an escort is never mentioned as a requirement.

qs.why: The text mentions “Cycling covers four kilometres in the time walking covers one”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable comparisons between bikes and walking, but the numbers and the text's direction are different: four kilometers versus one is not twice; “the stronger training effect for the heart” rejects the weaker exercise option; and “wet shoes” are actually a risk of walking over two kilometers.

qs.why: The text says beyond two kilometers cycling pays its costs “where a safe route exists, and is a poor idea where none does”.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are reasonable solutions for roads used by lorries, but the text blocks them: walking over two kilometers is said to take an hour a day, so it is not the faster one; adult accompaniment was never proposed; and keys are only part of the cost of cycling, not the answer for lanes shared with lorries.

qs.why: The text actually emphasizes that travel must be car-free, so the claim suggesting cars is the direct opposite of the closing sentence.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” is incorrect because the author rejects cars; “Not stated” is incorrect because the stance on cars is written explicitly.

qs.why: The text mentions “None of this difficulty is solved by lecturing individual shoppers about their choices”, then proposes spare parts obligations and lower tax rates.
