The claim about shade has the wrong SCOPE: its blocking phrase stands on its own, "Shade, it emerges, governs the pattern more powerfully than any single building material", acting as a mid-text finding, whereas the conclusion talks about accountability. The priority of planting has the wrong DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "Modelling indicates that planting achieves most where existing cover is thinnest"; that is a model result, and the text stops at citizen questions that are "harder to deflect", without demanding budget reallocations. The flaw in official tools has the wrong TARGET: it is used merely to explain why "official statistics rarely capture such a gap".

qs.why: Sensors are attached to garbage trucks which already have fixed routes to every neighborhood, so the device moves alongside routinely operating vehicles.
qs.whyOthersFail: Walking body height is the height at which sensors measure, not a modeling result; daily citizen reports appear as a consequence after data is published, not as a method of collection; and a single tool on open land is precisely the official measurement criticized for missing gaps between streets.

qs.why: The three-degree nighttime difference between mature tree-lined streets and barren streets is the most direct evidence for the shade claim.
qs.whyOthersFail: The widest temperature difference is said to occur precisely when resting bodies most need relief, namely at night, not in the afternoon; the eight-degree difference was measured at body height by researchers, not by official tools standing far from the street; and how sensors are transported is merely a matter of method, not evidence about shade.

qs.why: The clause "which is seldom where planting budgets have historically been directed" locks in the direction: the most barren places are rarely the targets of budgets.
qs.whyOthersFail: Compliance with sensor patterns is blocked by chronological order, because researchers "have therefore begun measuring" afterwards, so old budgets could not possibly have followed them, and the text calls it "seldom where planting budgets have historically been directed"; concentration on junctions and parking lots misreads the list "broad junctions, open car parks", which mentions places where heat accumulates, not where trees are planted; and the three-degree difference is limited by the text to "a mature avenue" compared to "a treeless equivalent", a single pair of streets, rather than most streets.

qs.why: The text states that official tools stand on open land and are deliberately kept away from traffic, so this claim is the reverse.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" clashes directly with that sentence; "Not stated" is wrong because the position of the tool is indeed mentioned.

qs.why: The report states that the financial case is robust based on those figures, yet still flags two risks and four recommendations that must be addressed.
qs.whyOthersFail: The complaint exceeding savings option clashes with complaints being spread across only a few streets; the objection already settled clashes with the recommendation to install new specifications on first-year streets; pausing the program clashes with next winter's scheduled completion date which remains maintained.

qs.why: The sequence is written explicitly in the recommendations list: "beginning with residential roads rather than main routes", and for dimming, "commission an independent assessment of dimming before extending it to any further streets". Thus, retrofitting new specifications starts on residential streets, while expanding dimming awaits an independent assessment.
qs.whyOthersFail: Expanding dimming first and assessing it later REVERSES the order requested by the report; the phrase "before extending it to any further streets" blocks it. Waiting for all light conversions to be completed before retrofitting a single first-year street GOES BEYOND the text: the report gives an eighteen-month deadline and never links it to the completion of conversions. Prioritizing main roads because complaints are higher there reverses priorities while also getting facts wrong: "Most of the letters come from a small number of roads", and the recommendation explicitly prioritizes residential streets.

qs.why: The locking sentence strictly forbids one logical step: "Officers should not assume public tolerance of dimming merely because complaints have been few". Thus, the stance is cautious, and quiet streets are not interpreted as approval.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are cautious and equally restrained, so their shape does not point to the key; the selector is the object of that restraint. Not demanding the reinstating of first-year streets has the wrong TARGET: the blocking phrase is the recommendation "Fit first-year streets with the revised specification within eighteen months". Rejecting credit for the revised specification also has the wrong TARGET: the blocking phrase is "which suggests the revision worked rather than that residents grew accustomed to the change". Caution primarily regarding tariffs has the wrong TARGET: tariffs are a separate primary risk, whereas for dimming the blocking phrase is "the evidence connecting that measure to reported feelings of safety remains thin".

qs.why: The signal has two parts in one sentence: savings are calculated against last financial year's tariffs, and a rise in unit prices will erode margins. Thus, that figure hangs upon the tariffs.
qs.whyOthersFail: Growth alongside conversion makes sense in the real world, but the text only links margins to unit prices, "a rise in unit prices would reduce the margin", without tying it to the number of lights; the possibility that maintenance visits lag behind calculations clashes with "maintenance visits have become markedly less frequent", which is actually used to support that figure; and third-party inspection is blocked by its status as a proposal, and that proposal is directed at dimming, not savings.

qs.why: "Two-thirds already converted" means the exact same thing as two out of three lights already replaced; only the unit of expression differs.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the numbers are the same; "Not stated" is wrong because that proportion is indeed written in the opening paragraph.

qs.why: Paragraph two states that walking does not yield comparable statistics, and what is uncounted in accepted units is treated as sentiment.
qs.whyOthersFail: The delay model option exaggerates time, clashing with the text which does not dispute the model's accuracy, only its scope; the deliberately hidden hierarchy clashes with “Nobody defends that hierarchy openly”, meaning inherited silence rather than conspiracy; main roads having to yield clashes with “None of this argues against major road works”.

qs.why: The text's comparison is indeed between eliminating danger for a thousand pedestrians a day and saving ninety seconds for four thousand cars.
qs.whyOthersFail: Buses only appear as vehicles splashing queues at bus stops, with no comparison of delays; schoolchild detour costs are figures the author proposes publishing later, not a comparison already in use; and the two cities are never compared in this text.

qs.why: The sentence about cities changing their rules is the clincher: "they simply stopped pretending the choice was technical rather than political", reinforced by "A preference dressed up as engineering necessity". What is criticized is the presentation of political choices as pure engineering.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are critical and two use the same restraint as the key register, so form does not distinguish them; the selectors are target and nuance. Willingness to let vehicle counts serve as the metric has the wrong TARGET: the blocking phrase is "Count pedestrians as carefully as vehicles". Reluctance to demand accountability has the wrong DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "The hierarchy will survive until somebody writes it down and asks who consented to it". The objection that preferences are defended too openly has the wrong NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "Nobody defends that hierarchy openly, and the silence is part of how it survives".

qs.why: The phrase "having attracted the traffic it was built to relieve" locks in the irony: what was supposed to be reduced is instead invited in.
qs.whyOthersFail: Counting pedestrians prior to approval is blocked by its status as a demand in the final paragraph, "Count pedestrians as carefully as vehicles", so it has never been done; the weakening reason for building again clashes directly with the clause "produces a fresh demand for another"; and funding from pavement budgets leaves no trace; the text only mentions pavement money as "postponed", without being redirected.

qs.why: Penulis menulis terang-terangan bahwa sebagian proyek jalan besar tak terhindarkan, jadi klaim ini kebalikan posisinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" clashes with that sentence; "Not stated" is wrong because the author's stance on major projects is stated directly.

qs.why: The final paragraph states that those records make planning much less speculative when used carefully alongside interviews and observation.
qs.whyOthersFail: The unnecessary interview option clashes with the condition “alongside interviews and street observation”; the ended dispute and hidden demand options are mentioned in the text, but both are supporting findings in paragraphs two and three, whereas the main conclusion concerns how to read them.

qs.why: A slightly delayed bus gathers more waiting passengers, loses time at every stop, and is then caught up by the bus behind it.
qs.whyOthersFail: Holding buses at stops for schedules makes sense in the real world, but the text does not mention it as a cause; manual two-week counts are old practices from before electronic ticketing, not causes of bunching; and extra-regional flows are actually separate findings about journeys passing through the city center.

qs.why: The pattern is called "familiar to passengers and long denied by operators", so that denial is not valued by the author: what refutes it is not new numerical data, but long-standing testimony.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are unimpressed and two claim to grant leeway, so the key register does not stand out; the selector is lexical signals. The allowance that mathematics is newly understood has the wrong NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "The cause is well understood mathematically". Objections primarily to center-bound travel models have the wrong TARGET: that is a separate finding on inter-district flows, whereas the blocking phrase for its refutation is "a pattern familiar to passengers and long denied by operators". Surrendering disputes to operators has the wrong DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "the argument about whether it existed simply ended".

qs.why: The concluding warning is paired: used carefully, those records improve planning, but made the final determinant, they merely repeat what is already baked into the network design.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are written in the same two-way contrast form, so the key is not uniquely elegant; each distractor shifts EXACTLY ONE element. The inter-district demand option shifts the CONSEQUENCE from assumption to demand figures, and is blocked by "they simply automate the assumptions already built into the network". The passenger belief option shifts the OWNER of the assumption, which in the text is the network. The replacing intent option shifts the SCOPE to another objection, "Card records show boardings, not intentions", which resides in another sentence and is not part of the concluding warning.

qs.why: "Bypassing the centre altogether" means the exact same thing as completely avoiding the city center.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because there is no refutation; "Not stated" is wrong because inter-district flows are mentioned explicitly.

qs.why: The phrase "What the exchange reveals is a mismatch of time horizons" is the author's own conclusion, and is immediately elaborated: merchants' difficulties are "immediate and specific", planners' benefits "gradual and general".
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors align with the thesis that both parties are sincere and their dispute is real, but miss the target or degree. Weakening merchant figures is blocked by "reasonably enough" and "Both cases deserve to be stated at full strength". The claim that consultation makes the scheme indefensible is blocked by "A scheme of this sort can still be defended, but only where the transition is funded rather than merely announced"; consultation questions council understanding, not the plan's validity. Disputes over the number of car-borne customers have the wrong TARGET: the blocking phrase is "What the exchange reveals is a mismatch of time horizons", not a numerical dispute.

qs.why: The planning department's enumeration states that most motorists arriving are through-traffic, not shoppers.
qs.whyOthersFail: Spend per visit is never calculated in the text, even though it is a reasonable argument for merchants to use; pre-nine-o'clock hours are loading rules in the plan, not enumeration findings; and the comparison is reversed, because pedestrians are stated to outnumber car passengers nine to one.

qs.why: The concluding sentence states, "on the evidence of its consultation", it is unclear whether the council grasped that distinction; thus the consultation itself is what is questioned in adequacy.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are unimpressed and two offer leeway similar to the key, so cross-questioning does not resolve it; selectors are target and degree. Objections primarily to media coverage have the wrong TARGET: coverage is indeed rebuked, but the blocking phrase is "on the evidence of its consultation", which points to the council. The allowance that online forms reach both parties has the wrong NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "consultation took place through an online form during a fortnight in August", which is noted as a fair objection. The satisfaction that funded transitions are available has the wrong DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "only where the transition is funded rather than merely announced".

qs.why: The phrase "poor compensation for a rent due in March" locks in the mismatch: gradual benefits do not cover bills falling due.
qs.whyOthersFail: Cafe recoveries reaching them is blocked by "gradual benefits are poor compensation for a rent due in March" plus "a temporary decline in trade followed by a slow recovery"; granting loading permits fails because the text states the department "has offered" permits specifically for furniture merchants, with no recipients described; and acceptance after revenue recovers clashes with the author's condition, "only where the transition is funded rather than merely announced".

qs.why: The nearest sentence merely explains the contents of the plan and loading hours; the reason why the plan was created is never stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" requires a cause absent from the text; "False" is also wrong because the text denies no causes.

qs.why: Paragraph two states that its design rests on features of human attention: small recurring costs are ignored and their monitoring is vastly overestimated.
qs.whyOthersFail: The options of placement for terms and a firm option that better understands shopping lists are indeed text sentences, but both are props, not the thesis; the household audit option shifts the burden to customers, whereas the text places the primary remedy on rules for firms.

qs.why: The cited survey states that people underestimate their monthly obligations by about a third, so roughly one pound out of every three pounds that must be paid.
qs.whyOthersFail: The direction of the difference is actually reversed, because the text mentions the widest gap in households with the narrowest room; the cost of a single renewal notice is never used as a measure; and four pounds is an example of a small bill, not the magnitude of the difference.

qs.why: The concluding sentence of paragraph four provides the anchor: "those relying on inattention will object loudly, and their objection is itself the evidence". Loud objections are read as evidence, not as complaints that need to be weighed.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are skeptical and two of them use the same measurable leniency as the key, so guessing the thesis does not help; the differentiator is target and degree. The leniency on compliance costs is wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrases are "Firms confident of their value have little to fear from such rules" and "Regulation here need not be heavy". The accusation of hiding terms is also wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "every term appears somewhere in the agreement"; what is contested is the placement. The willingness to allow cancellation placement is wrong in TARGET: the blocking phrase is "Require that cancellation be no harder than subscription".

qs.why: Two consecutive signals: cancellation is "rarely on the page where the subscription began" and reminders are "seldom sent". Such design counts on customers forgetting to opt out.
qs.whyOthersFail: The obligation of a reminder that might already be in effect is blocked by the proposal list in the final paragraph, "that a reminder precede any annual renewal", so there is no rule yet; the intention to bill outside the agreement falls apart at "None of this is fraud; every term appears somewhere in the agreement"; and the habit of canceling on the registration page collides with the words "rarely on the page where the subscription began".

qs.why: The author asserts this practice is not fraud and all terms are written down, so claims about breaking the law contradict this.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" collides directly with that sentence; "Not stated" is wrong because the legal status is specifically discussed.

qs.why: The final paragraph mentions the roster as safety equipment that must be seriously designed, following two paragraphs measuring the cost of night work.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option to end night work collides with "None of this argues for the abolition of night work"; the option of full circadian adjustment collides with "complies slowly, incompletely, and never for good"; the option of thin supervision as a cause collides with the errors referred to as predictable roster outputs.

qs.why: The text states the sharpest drop occurs between three and five in the morning, so roughly four o'clock.
qs.whyOthersFail: A long sequence in a single pattern is actually said to allow partial adjustment, not the worst decline; morning light after night shifts is cited as helping recovery; and the first hour of a shift is never called the worst point.

qs.why: The concluding sentence shifts the burden: "Where they have not, the cost is still paid, simply by somebody else". Thus, employers who allow the roster to remain are considered to owe for that cost.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options criticize employers and three of them hold back or grant leniency, so the key's format is no longer distinctive; the differentiator is lexical signals. The acceptance that the punishing nature of rosters is inevitable is wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrases are "Not every rota is equally punishing" and "These are cheap adjustments". The reluctance to demand roster redesign is wrong in TARGET: the blocking phrase is "the rota is a piece of safety equipment, and should be designed with the same seriousness as any other". The hope that cheap adjustments are now commonplace is wrong in NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "they are frequently the last to be considered".

qs.why: Penanda kontras "whereas" memisahkan dua nasib: rangkaian panjang memberi penyesuaian sebagian, minggu bergantian "prevents any adjustment at all".
qs.whyOthersFail: Compatibility with worker preferences is blocked by the opening sentence rejecting that framework, "Shift work is often discussed as a matter of preference... Laboratory evidence suggests something considerably less negotiable"; minimizing the pattern compared to total hours fails because the text places total hours below light access, rather than above pattern; and the claim of being more tolerable collides with "shifts advancing forwards... are tolerated better than those which jump backwards", so the direction is actually reversed.

qs.why: "Instructions chiefly from light" itu parafrasa langsung: penanda waktunya terutama cahaya.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because there is no rebuttal; "Not stated" is wrong because the role of light is explicitly mentioned in the first paragraph.

qs.why: The anchor is the sentence "We recommend that the department require annual publication of grade distributions ... together with the number of offers made on contextual grounds", which unites the three previous arguments into a single piece of advice: publish more completely.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors repeat real parts of the paper's thesis (openness is good) and two of them use the same advisory register as the key; what separates them is scope and degree. The proposal to fund applicant behavior studies is wrong in SCOPE: the blocking phrase is "The department should also fund one longitudinal study", marked by "also" as an addition to the main recommendation "We recommend that the department require annual publication of grade distributions". The warning about league tables is wrong in TARGET: the blocking phrase is "That risk is real, though it argues for publishing alongside a measure of progress after entry, not for publishing nothing". Lowering entry requirements is wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "None of this asks a single institution to lower its bar".

qs.why: What is withheld is precisely the grade distribution among admitted students, meaning how widely their scores differ.
qs.whyOthersFail: The proportion of rejected applicants is never part of the discussed dataset; the number of applications and offers is actually said to be published already; and entry requirements are advertised, sometimes even higher than what is truly accepted.

qs.why: Kalimatnya mengakui lalu mengalihkan: "That risk is real, though it argues for publishing alongside a measure of progress after entry, not for publishing nothing", dan ditutup "A bad table is a reason to build a better one".
qs.whyOthersFail: Three options acknowledge the risk is real and draw a measurable conclusion, so the key's register does not stand out; the differentiator is the text's chosen solution. The accusation of institutional protection motives is wrong in NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "That risk is real", an acknowledgment, not an exposure of motives. Withholding contextual offer figures is wrong in TARGET: the blocking phrase is "together with the number of offers made on contextual grounds". Delegating publication to prospectuses is wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "Publication should be centralized in a single register rather than left to individual prospectuses".

qs.why: Klausa "rests more on principle than on evidence about behaviour" mengunci timbangannya, dan studinya masih berupa permintaan pendanaan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Completed studies are blocked by the phrase "The department should also fund one longitudinal study", meaning it hasn't been done yet; the origin of evidence from small classes fails because small classes appear in the privacy objection, "without effectively identifying individuals", not as a data source; and collection prior to advice requests has no trace whatsoever in the text.

qs.why: "Centralized in a single register" has the same meaning as gathered in a single central list.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because there is no rejection; "Not stated" is wrong because the recommendation is clearly written.

qs.why: The concluding sentence states the proposal merely stops useful internal habits from being sold to the public as finished products.
qs.whyOthersFail: The journal review weakness option is paragraph two's premise, not its thesis; the server option as the only thing that must change collides with the responsibility called "shared" between servers, institutions, and reporters; the option of institutions stopping announcements is one of three suggestions, not the conclusion.

qs.why: The text states preprints carry no markers usable by the general public, and the phrase 'unreviewed' does not work in news headlines.
qs.whyOthersFail: Records of who commented are indeed not part of preprints, but the text never mentions them as missing; the scope of corrections is a consequence in the reporting realm, not something that should be in the preprint itself; and fast servers are readily available, which is why papers can be published within hours.

qs.why: There are two anchor phrases: journal review as a guarantee of truth is called "a comfortable fiction", and anyone who has seen a reviewed paper retracted knows the seal is not worth as much as readers assume.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are unimpressed by journal reviews and two of them grant leniency or hold back like the key, so their format does not separate them; the differentiator is target and nuance. Leniency regarding drafts that need translation is wrong in TARGET: the blocking phrase is "The difficulty lies not in posting but in translation", meaning prepublication difficulty, not the nature of the review. Gratitude for filtering is wrong in NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "treating it as a guarantee of truth was always a comfortable fiction". Willingness to let the seal stand as a signal is wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrases are "the seal was never worth what readers assumed" and the proposal "servers could readily require a plain statement of what remains untested".

qs.why: Frasa "reaches a fraction of the original audience" mengunci jangkauannya: sebagian besar pembaca berita pertama tak pernah menemuinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: The same audience is blocked by "the correction, when it comes, reaches a fraction of the original audience"; designating reporters as correction publishers fails because the text is silent on who issues them and only asks journalists to withhold the word "shows"; and rapid trust recovery collides with "Trust is spent at the moment of announcement and can only be repaid slowly".

qs.why: The author states the practice's benefits are real and should not be abandoned, so this claim contradicts their position.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" collides with that sentence; "Not stated" is wrong because their stance on continuing the practice is stated directly.

qs.why: The text concludes that the choice of measurement itself is a policy, after showing that what wakes people up are events, not averages.
qs.whyOthersFail: The cheapest treatment option is a supporting finding in paragraph three, not the thesis; the unlawful resident option reverses the value of the sentence “legally sound and beside the point”; the undeveloped science option collides with “That is not a scientific difficulty, since the measurements exist”.

qs.why: The sleeping body is said to respond to changes, specifically the surge from a quiet background to the sound of a passing train.
qs.whyOthersFail: Train counts do matter, but the text links them to nighttime awakenings, not daytime traffic; daily noise energy is precisely what the body does not perceive; and regulatory averages are the measurements being criticized.

qs.why: Two tracks with the same average can produce vastly different nights; that is the most direct proof that averages are misleading.
qs.whyOthersFail: Barriers and rail grinding are handling choices, not proof of average flaws; and the fact that regulations are written around average figures merely explains the origin of the problem, not that the figures are wrong.

qs.why: A single sentence contains two directions at once, "improves the average while worsening exactly the events that matter": the numbers improve, the nights worsen.
qs.whyOthersFail: Reductions in both measures are blocked by the second half of that sentence, "while worsening exactly the events that matter"; upper-floor resident satisfaction is misplaced, because upper floors appear regarding barriers, "Barriers help, but chiefly for the upper floors"; and the elimination of maintenance needs collides with "The most effective single measure, according to several studies, is maintenance".

qs.why: The closest sentence merely connects waking up to train counts; comparisons between freight and passenger trains are never made.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" requires a comparison not found in the text; "False" is also wrong because the text does not deny that comparison.

qs.why: The conclusion the author calls honest: recordings redistribute, widening access to information while narrowing access to the unscheduled.
qs.whyOthersFail: The attendance numbers never measure learning option is the first department head's argument, not the author's conclusion; both reading different figures collides with “the same figures” and with the dispute described as interpretive; the department recording without changing anything is a consequence drawn after the conclusion, not the conclusion itself.

qs.why: He mentions students working two night shifts, those caring for family, and those commuting ninety minutes each way.
qs.whyOthersFail: The least connected student is the group observed by the second department head, not him; choosing to study in one's own time is never the reason, because his argument concerns time limits, not preferences; and withdrawal is called a risk to be prevented, not the students' current state.

qs.why: The author weighs both positions ("each is arguing from something real") then passes judgment: "A department that records everything and changes nothing else has made a choice without admitting it", as does the one refusing to record.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options accept that both positions make sense and two of them hold back like the key, so the cross-question thesis does not choose; the differentiator is its concluding lexical signal. Partiality to the access case is wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "Both accounts rest on evidence chosen to fit the expectation each observer brought to it". Satisfaction in letting both conclusions stand is wrong in NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "The honest conclusion is that recordings redistribute something rather than simply adding it", a conclusion drawn by the author themselves. Reluctance to urge either department to change is wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "Institutional honesty, on this reading, demands an explicit justification rather than an inherited arrangement".

qs.why: The phrase "So has" copies the previous sentence's accusation onto the recording-refusing department: both choose without admitting it.
qs.whyOthersFail: The claim that unscheduled meetings are saved is blocked by the words "calls the result community", meaning a label rather than proof; the return of attendance numbers fails at the opening "attendance in many departments has not recovered" after three years; and evidence-based superiority collides with "Both accounts rest on evidence chosen to fit the expectation each observer brought to it".

qs.why: "Accepts every word of that" has the same meaning as agreeing with the colleague's portrayal of student conditions.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because that agreement is written; "Not stated" is wrong because the sentence exists, just phrased differently.

qs.why: The text states no one designed that outcome: it followed the installed goal, namely seconds of attention.
qs.whyOthersFail: Adolescent vulnerability options are paragraph three premises used to explain the mechanism, not the main claim; age verification options are examples of missing the target, not the thesis; indifferent firms collide with “Nobody designed this outcome” and with engineers described as doing tasks according to specification.

qs.why: The text states what is optimized is measured in seconds of attention, meaning how long people keep watching.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sharing with friends makes sense as a goal for systems like this, but the text never mentions it; intensity is called a trait of winning content in competition, not the optimized magnitude; and account age is just an entry gate matter that the text says answers the wrong question.

qs.why: The anchor sentence is "The impossibility is not technical; it is commercial, and it should be named as such", preceded by the note that firms formulate comparable quarterly objectives. Thus, that claim is read as revenue defense.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options reject the firm's claim and the three distractors grant leniency or hold back, so the key's register does not stand out; the differentiator is target and degree. The leniency that formulating objectives is difficult is wrong in NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "they specify comparable objectives every quarter, in language precise enough to pay bonuses on". The leniency that age verification answers part of the difficulty is wrong in TARGET: the blocking phrase is "A gate answers the wrong question, since the difficulty begins after entry". The willingness to let each firm name its own objective is wrong in DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "require the chosen objective to be published".

qs.why: The metaphor "gate" plus the clause "the difficulty begins after entry" locks in its working limits: the door is regulated, the bait content is not.
qs.whyOthersFail: The downplaying of teen attention value is blocked by "A gate answers the wrong question, since the difficulty begins after entry", because the duration target remains intact after people enter; the comparison between young and old users is never made in the text, which only mentions teens are "more sensitive to social comparison"; and the firm's proposal collides with "Regulators have responded with age verification", which frames it as a regulatory step.

qs.why: The text directly refutes this: dangerous material is not promoted intentionally.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" contradicts that sentence; "Not stated" is wrong because the refutation is written at the start of the second paragraph.

qs.why: Paragraf pertama menyebut partisipasi bergeser puluhan poin persen begitu bentuk formulirnya berubah, dan penjelasan lewat preferensi tak pernah pulih.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of increased participation without increased contributions and the option of printed figures read as encouragement are both details from paragraph three about downstream consequences, not the main finding; the option that workers rarely move from low tariffs is a symptom of inertia used to explain, not the claim.

qs.why: One of the three things brought by default arrangements is a signal of what employers consider normal.
qs.whyOthersFail: The previous choice note is never called part of the default arrangement; pre-agreed contributions collide with the picture of workers accepting whatever figure is printed on the form; and cross-country replication is the status of the finding, not the content of the regulation.

qs.why: The text accepts automatic enrolment as a working finding, then withholds praise: "Workers enrolled at three per cent often remain at three per cent for a decade, treating the figure as advice rather than a floor".
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options agree with the mechanism and three of them use the same measurable anxiety, so the key form is no longer distinct; the decider is target and degree. The concern that the effect fades misses the TARGET and contradicts the text: the blocking phrase is "it does not fade after the first year". The objection that defaults oppress choice misses the TARGET: the blocking phrase is "There is no arrangement without a default, because somebody must determine what happens when nothing is determined". The belief that three per cent suits most workers misses the NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "the contribution rate accompanying automatic enrolment is frequently minimal".

qs.why: The locking sentence closes off possibilities: there must always be a rule for what happens when nobody decides.
qs.whyOthersFail: Accuracy in revealing preferences is blocked by the opening paragraph, since "the tidy account of preference has never fully recovered"; the rise in participation across firms of all sizes is a result of opt-out defaults, "The effect shows up in firms of every size", not the absence of regulation; and cross-country testing concerns "The finding has since been replicated", namely the opt-in versus opt-out findings.

qs.why: The text only says employers started changing that detail; who first proposed it is never mentioned.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" fabricates the source of the idea; "False" is also wrong because the text does not deny the role of government economists, it is silent on the matter.

qs.why: The word "also" reverses the opening paragraph: "It has also delivered a distribution of benefit that the council did not intend and cannot easily defend", and the three amendments at the end fix the direction of payments, not the amount.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors repeat real parts of the report's content, but are wrong in scope or degree. Recording success misses the NUANCE: the blocking phrase is the word "also" in "It has also delivered a distribution of benefit that the council did not intend", which frames target achievement as background. Establishing that tenants are the excluded group misses the SCOPE: the blocking phrase is the third amendment, "commission an assessment of the split arrangements before extending them here", so the tenant issue is actually postponed, and per-ward distribution remains the main finding. The request for new funds misses the DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "None of the changes below needs new money, only a different order of payment".

qs.why: The scheme requires applicants to cover thousands of pounds upfront and wait eleven weeks before reimbursement.
qs.whyOthersFail: The four lowest-income wards are actually still allowed to apply, just with amounts below seven percent; installer reluctance is never mentioned in the report; and exceeding capacity targets is a success of the scheme, not a barrier for applicants.

qs.why: Below seven percent of all applications means less than one in fourteen, which directly points to uneven benefits.
qs.whyOthersFail: The eleven-week deadline and the forty percent share explain the reason for that pattern through payment design, rather than showing distribution; and the number of installations only describes the scale of the scheme, which the report uses to call it successful on other measures.

qs.why: The locking sentence sets a condition: without the first proposal, the remaining two change almost nothing, and that first proposal is what removes the initial capital requirement.
qs.whyOthersFail: The removal of direct payments is blocked by "Without the first amendment, the remaining two will change very little", because the dependency order is actually the reverse; the certainty of savings passed on to tenants fails at "the passed-through saving in both pilots remains unverified"; and a surge in installation numbers was never promised, since the report states the scheme has already "exceeded its capacity target".

qs.why: "Excluded almost entirely" has the same meaning as nearly completely closed off to tenants.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the text states the same thing; "Not stated" is wrong because the tenants' situation is discussed throughout the third paragraph.

qs.why: The first paragraph states that universities buy the visible part of teaching and receive the rest as a gift.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option that preparation multipliers are too low is a detail from paragraph two, and the text actually states those who accept the principle only argue over the amount; the option of training for unpaid work tolerance is a consequence in paragraph three; the option of capping student numbers is a single remedy item in the final paragraph.

qs.why: Contract multipliers are usually two while the honest figure is closer to four, so roughly half of the actual need.
qs.whyOthersFail: The multiplier is mentioned for preparation, while assignment checking is proposed to be paid per script; midnight messages are examples of work falling outside counted hours; and abolishing the multiplier collides with the sentence that contracts often include it.

qs.why: The locking phrase is the training table of contents: "Training implies observation, feedback and a reduction in load while competence is built, and few of these appear on any timetable". So the argument is rejected because the promised content is mostly absent.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options reject that defense and the three distractors grant leeway or hold back like the key, so cross-question thesis selection does not help; the decider is target and degree. The objection primarily to the multiplier size misses the TARGET: the two-versus-four multiplier is a rebuttal regarding preparation hours, and the blocking phrase for the training argument remains "few of these appear on any timetable". The reluctance to demand a four-hour count misses the DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "count preparation honestly" along with "the honest figure is nearer four". Handing the difference over to the budget misses the NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "Budgets have permitted the present arrangement precisely because somebody else has been absorbing the difference".

qs.why: The phrase "precisely because" points to the reason: the budget can afford it precisely because the difference is absorbed by someone else, namely unpaid work.
qs.whyOthersFail: Budget inability is an excuse quoted from the department, "Departments will reply that budgets do not permit it", and immediately dismantled by the locking sentence; postgraduate involvement in budget preparation is never mentioned; and payment per script remains a proposal, "pay marking by the script rather than by the hour".

qs.why: Penulis justru menyebut perbaikannya mahal walau sederhana, jadi klaim ini berlawanan.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" contradicts the opening sentence of the final paragraph; "Not stated" is wrong because the cost is stated directly.

qs.why: Paragraph two states the sensor network reports moisture continuously, and combining this with forecasts significantly improves flood prediction.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option that urban soil is too diverse is a complication in paragraph three which the text says does not make this approach a poor investment; the maintenance commitment option and forecast value option depending on city actions are both conditions in the final paragraph, not its core findings. | "the forecast improves only where the sensors ..." is wrong: inspection concerns the drifting sensors, while the text ties the forecast's worth to where warnings are acted upon | "the hardware price is what makes such a netwo..." is wrong: the text says 'None of this makes the approach a poor investment' and the real costs never appear in the hardware price

qs.why: Soil that has already absorbed water acts like pavement when a storm arrives: almost no water enters.
qs.whyOthersFail: Drying speed compared to pavement is never discussed; greater absorption is the exact opposite of that sentence; and sensor drift is described as an inherent device defect, unrelated to wet soil.

qs.why: Satu daerah tangkapan air memotong separuh peringatan palsu tanpa melewatkan satu peringatan sungguhan; itu bukti manfaat paling langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Non-stop reporting only explains how the device works; whereas soil diversity and reading drift are two complications that actually reduce network value, not support it.

qs.why: The phrase "a flood they will handle exactly as before" locks in the result: forecasts improve, handling does not, and the closing adds "A better number is only worth as much as the city does with it".
qs.whyOthersFail: More frequent missed warnings are blocked by the opposite report statement, "without any warning being missed"; avoiding inspection costs fails at "neither of which appears in the price of the hardware", so those costs are still pending; and reducing sensor redundancy collides with "A network therefore requires redundancy and routine inspection".

qs.why: "Drifting rather than stopping" means readings deviate slowly, and the text notes that is harder to detect.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the content aligns with the text; "Not stated" is wrong because the nature of sensor failure is explained in the third paragraph.

qs.why: The locking sentence states two things at once: "We recommend continuation with three conditions", and those three conditions are detailed in the same paragraph.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors repeat real parts of this memo, but are wrong in scope or degree. The value of long records misses the SCOPE: the blocking phrase is the next sentence, "That argument does not justify preserving the network unchanged", so it is a step in the reasoning, not the memo's goal. Tendering the oxygen contract also misses the SCOPE: it is one of three conditions in "We recommend continuation with three conditions". The request for additional funds misses the DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "The cost of all three measures falls well within the existing allocation".

qs.why: The text states that gaps in the record cannot be filled later, so a lost year is gone forever.
qs.whyOthersFail: Insurers are mentioned as data series users, not payers per reading; installation years are just background on network age; and telemetry's ability to measure oxygen is never discussed, the text only states telemetry reduces visits.

qs.why: A fifty-year series enables estimating how often a given flood height repeats, and that is the strongest reason to maintain existing stations.
qs.whyOthersFail: Already closed channels are actually used as the reason to close three stations, rather than keep them; whereas calibration schedules and visit reductions concern operating costs, not the value of long records.

qs.why: The locking signal is "smaller than suppliers imply", which places supplier figures above actual figures once installation costs are calculated.
qs.whyOthersFail: Comparisons with calibration contract costs are never made, and the locking sentence actually minimizes savings, "the saving is smaller than suppliers imply once installation is counted"; funding repairs for four stations fails because all proposed costs are said to fall "well within the existing allocation", without being linked to telemetry savings; and the link to closing oxygen sites collides with the memo's own proposal, which only asks to retender the contract.

qs.why: The text only says costs remain within the existing allocation; the monitoring budget portion is never given a figure.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" adds a number that isn't there; "False" is also wrong because the text does not deny that portion, it is simply silent.

qs.why: The closing sentence states transition costs are left to settle on those least able to debate them.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of shops choosing customers and the option of administrative exclusion are both from paragraph three sentences, illustrating how those costs are distributed; the option of terminal costs on small transactions is an example from paragraph two, and the text notes they are small individually but large in aggregate.

qs.why: Merchants who buy goods every morning cannot wait for funds to clear, whereas card payments take three business days.
qs.whyOthersFail: Terminal rent is called a fixed cost, unrelated to settlement duration; percentage fees on two-pound purchases are specifically called not trivial; and what clears instantly is cash, not cards.

qs.why: The locking phrase is "it has quietly selected its customers" followed by "That decision is seldom announced in those terms": the choice is real but unrecognized as a choice.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are critical of the transition and the three distractors grant leeway or hold back, so guessing the thesis does not help; the decider is target and degree. The willingness to leave terminal costs uncapped misses the DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "Terminal fees on small transactions could be capped". The objection primarily to the settlement deadline misses the TARGET: that is a merchant burden, whereas this issue concerns shops, and the blocking phrase is "A shop that stops accepting cash has not merely changed its systems; it has quietly selected its customers". The satisfaction that changes are announced misses the NUANCE: the blocking phrase is "That decision is seldom announced in those terms".

qs.why: Klausa "which does not fall on the people who design it" menyingkirkan perancangnya, dan penutup menaruh biayanya "on those least able to argue about it".
qs.whyOthersFail: System designers are specifically excluded by the clause "which does not fall on the people who design it"; existing cardholders fails because the focus is "one adult in twenty here has no usable card"; and merchants with generous margins collide with their own example, "a market trader selling vegetables on small margins".

qs.why: The author firmly states that their writing is not a reason to freeze payment technology.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" contradicts the opening sentence of the final paragraph; "Not stated" is wrong because its position is stated explicitly.

qs.why: Reviewer's conclusion: limits combined with development are a policy distinct from limits alone, so the details determine the outcome.
qs.whyOthersFail: The relocation footprint option is the first researcher's evidence; the unbuilt flat option is the second researcher's argument; the question of which loss is harder to reverse is the formulation of the dispute in paragraph one, whereas the reviewer concludes with specification, not vocabulary.

qs.why: The household moved to a worse flat, a longer commute, or a room in a relative's house.
qs.whyOthersFail: Stricter enforcement appears in the final paragraph as a design detail, not as a tenant's action; moving to a cheaper city is directly refuted by the text; and delayed repairs are the landlord's action in the second researcher's argument.

qs.why: He points to quietly deferred maintenance and unofficial payments that emerge when legal rent is withheld below the market rate.
qs.whyOthersFail: A twenty-percent increase for fixed-income and long-term former tenants in schools and jobs are two pieces of evidence from the first researcher, which actually support limits; and strict enforcement across most of the market is never claimed in the text, it is merely called one of the details that determines the outcome.

qs.why: The locking sentence states the consequence directly: arguing about words makes the same evidence usable by both parties.
qs.whyOthersFail: The resolution of the debate is blocked by "The honest position is that both effects are real"; enforcement as the single determinant fails on "Specification, not vocabulary, determines the empirical outcome", because enforcement is only one of three details; and the superiority of the long-term view collides with the reviewer's placement of "the first year of a cap" and "the eighth" as two equally real concerns.

qs.why: "Share a dataset" means they indeed worked from the same set of figures.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the text states the same thing; "Not stated" is wrong because data sharing is mentioned in the first paragraph.

qs.why: The word "therefore" connects all evidence to one proposal: "a floor calculated on engaged time, set with reference to the statutory minimum plus an allowance for costs", namely time actually spent working.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors repeat a real part of this paper, but miss the scope or degree. Testing the operator departure fails in SCOPE: the blocking phrase is "Neither objection survives contact with the comparative evidence", making it an answered objection rather than a goal. Setting the waiting-time portion also fails in SCOPE: it is intermediate evidence, and the blocking phrase is "We therefore recommend", which makes it a step toward the proposal. The quarterly reporting obligation fails in DEGREE: in the recommendation sentence it is a complement, marked by "together with".

qs.why: What is rejected is data about application check-in times without orders, namely the waiting hours that are precisely the subject of dispute.
qs.whyOthersFail: The number of new recruitments appears in the recommendation as something that needs to be visible, not something rejected; gross earnings per hour are actually available and already compared with the minimum wage; and insurance and vehicle costs are stated to be borne by drivers, with no data dispute.

qs.why: Earnings after costs and waiting time are no longer comparable to the minimum wage, and that is the most direct basis for the base fare.
qs.whyOthersFail: The burden of insurance explains part of the cause of that gap, not showing the gap itself; operator departure is used to defeat the second objection; and the objection regarding flexibility is the argument of opponents of the base fare.

qs.why: The phrase "leaves an incentive to over-recruit" locks the consequence, and the second half of the sentence explains why the reporting obligation remains necessary.
qs.whyOthersFail: The removal of the reporting obligation is blocked by the second half of that sentence, "the disclosure duty is what makes that visible"; operator departure fails on "Both operators making that argument have remained in jurisdictions where floors were introduced"; and the loss of flexibility collides with "a floor applied to engaged time alone would leave logging in unrestricted".

qs.why: The text actually states that legal status is not the question being answered.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" collides with that sentence; "Not stated" is wrong because the refusal to discuss legal status is explicitly mentioned.

qs.why: The text mentions an instructive core: the two do not disagree on accuracy, and what remains unanswered is cognitive.
qs.whyOthersFail: The returning-time option is the first clinician's case; the option of writing notes as a place where judgment forms is the second clinician's objection; the option that both illustrate different parts of work is the introduction of paragraph one, not the point asserted by the author.

qs.why: Dua jam menjadi dua puluh menit, jadi pekerjaan malamnya tinggal sekitar seperenam waktu semula.
qs.whyOthersFail: Two hours is the old state before the device was used, not correction time; sending summaries to colleagues is said to become clearer, without a time reference; and writing from scratch by oneself is precisely what she abandons.

qs.why: The author calls the variable "cognitive rather than administrative" and concludes with "Until that question is settled, a practice adopting such a system is running an experiment on its own judgement": the objection is weighty and unanswered.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options treat the objection as serious and two distractors provide leeway or withhold judgment like the key, so register does not separate them; the differentiators are degree and target. The assumption that it is already resolved by savings fails in DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "The unresolved variable is cognitive rather than administrative". Narrowing it down to accuracy concern fails in TARGET: the blocking phrase is "they are not disagreeing about accuracy". The willingness to let the shift go unelaborated fails in DEGREE: the blocking phrase is "A cautious practice would insist that the displacement be described in advance".

qs.why: The word "conceals" locks the direction: fluency conceals uncertainty rather than revealing it.
qs.whyOthersFail: The ease of finding errors is blocked by the following sentence which reverses the direction, "a fluent error is harder to detect than an awkward one"; the shorter draft fails on the first clinician's report, "longer and more thorough than the one she wrote herself"; and the loss of the requirement to sign collides with "He has twice signed a draft".

qs.why: The text only says patients notice the change; satisfaction levels before and after are never compared.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" concludes a comparison that does not exist; "False" is also wrong because the text does not deny patient satisfaction, it is silent on its magnitude.

qs.why: The first paragraph mentions a hard-to-avoid conclusion: memory resembles reconstruction more than playback.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of a one-time effort that keeps paying off is a response to the criticism in paragraph three; the willpower-based advice and the institution testing patience are both consequences drawn in paragraph four, not claims supporting the entire essay.

qs.why: Bedanya cuma letak ponsel: satu di meja dekat buku, satu ditinggal di lemari kamar lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: The silent/off option sounds like a sensible study trick, but the text never discusses sound mode; the only distinction made is “face down on the desk” versus “in a drawer in a separate room”. The study-time option adds an artificial difference; the text says both face the same test. The motivation option actually collides directly with “equally weak motivation” in the opening sentence of the example.

qs.why: All four options accord the objection equal respect; the text selects its degree: the objection is called worth hearing, room arrangement is acknowledged as a choice, and the author still concludes that the objection confuses the moment of effort with its location.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors align with the thesis that room arrangement defeats willpower, equally respecting the objection, and all three also restrain themselves after that respect, so the key's form is no longer distinctive. Softening the argument is blocked by "Nevertheless, the objection confuses the moment of effort with its location", because not a single claim is withdrawn and "Effort invested once in a sensible arrangement continues to repay the investment for weeks". Reluctance to blame institutions fails in TARGET: the objection comes from critics, whereas regarding institutions the author is firm: "Institutions distributing cheerful reminders about determination, while tolerating noisy classrooms and chaotic timetables, are examining patience rather than cultivating it". Leaving it open is blocked by the rebuttal provided in the very next sentence.

qs.why: The institution permits “noisy classrooms and chaotic timetables” while demanding persistence, so what they do is “examining patience rather than cultivating it”; students are tested through obstacles that are never removed.
qs.whyOthersFail: The cost option is the most natural explanation for any school and is hedged by "may", but the text does not mention money at all and concludes with "nobody considered moving them", which is a matter of attention, not budget. The family option also makes sense in the real world, but what the text mentions is only space, schedule, and devices that were "arranged against her", all under the institution's control. The finding about diligent students sounds like a normal evaluation result, but the text says such advice "fails exactly those who ask for help", and no findings are reported.

qs.why: The text actually states that a one-time organizing effort pays off for weeks, whereas fighting cues every night pays off nothing. This claim reverses its polarity.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the direction of the statement is opposite; "Not stated" is wrong because the comparison is written precisely in one sentence.

qs.why: All four options mention the same task, which is questioning something; the text specifies its target: "What merits suspicion is not the questionnaire but the certainty it invites".
qs.whyOthersFail: All three question elements genuinely present in the essay's thesis, and each misses the target. Questioning the instrument is blocked by the same sentence, since what is suspected is not the questionnaire, and blocked by "Careful instruments do predict conduct modestly". Questioning the sense of relief is blocked by "recognition can bring genuine relief when a private pattern is finally named", because that is explicitly acknowledged. Questioning score shifts is blocked by its own usage, because the shift is the author's evidence, not what he suspects.

qs.why: The text says scores frequently shift, especially when employment, health, or friendships change.
qs.whyOthersFail: The fixed-score option is people's reasonable assumption about personality tests, but the text clearly writes that scores “frequently drifts”. The shift-to-the-center option mixes another sentence: what is described as close to the midpoint is some people's position across many dimensions, not the shift direction after two years. The stable-health option reverses the condition, because the text actually mentions changes in “employment, health or friendships” as triggers for the shift.

qs.why: The concrete example: a student labeled an introvert stops signing up for debate club because it feels dishonest.
qs.whyOthersFail: The manager option is indeed a precise detail from the text, but it is an office example, not proof that a student's choices narrow down. The shifting-score option is actually used by the text to counter the type concept, so its direction does not connect with the stem. The midpoint option describes how researchers map traits, and mentions not a single consequence for students.

qs.why: The text says he and the student “have acquired an excuse to stop observing”, so the label replaces the work of paying attention to people rather than adding to it.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of learning who is capable sounds like a normal manager's result, and the hedge "perhaps" does not help it, because the text concludes: "Neither has discovered anything genuinely new about the pupil or the department". The company-mandated option is a very plausible office story, but the text mentions no orders or policies whatsoever; he merely "reads that his department consists of thinkers and feelers". The department-becoming-more-open option is also reasonably believed to be a benefit of labels, but what the text reports is the opposite, namely difficult conversations thrown at the badge-holder matching them.

qs.why: This is a paraphrase of the sentence acknowledging that careful measuring tools do predict behavior modestly.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the text actually acknowledges it; "Not stated" is wrong because that acknowledgment is clearly written.

qs.why: The first paragraph mentions a hard-to-avoid conclusion: memory is more like reconstruction than playback.
qs.whyOthersFail: The single-word-entering-the-record option is the film experiment in paragraph two that supports the claim; the detail-discarding option is the explanation of why reconstruction is not a flaw; the first-interview option is the procedural lesson in paragraph four.

qs.why: They reported broken glass that never actually appeared in the film.
qs.whyOthersFail: The lower-speed option reverses the effect's direction: a harsher word raises estimates, not lowers them. The previously forgotten glass option sounds reasonable, but the text firmly states the glass “never appeared in the film”, so it is not about forgetting. The already mentioned detail does not answer the stem, because what is interesting is the new report appearing a week later.

qs.why: The procedure is sequential: one short film for all participants, then "half of them are asked how fast the vehicles were travelling when they smashed; the remainder hear the milder verb hit", and "A week later" both groups are asked to report what they saw.
qs.whyOthersFail: Two different films contradict "Both groups had watched exactly the same short film", and the glass "never appeared in the film". The option making word variation depend on who mentions the glass REVERSES cause and effect: the word is inserted beforehand then "has been folded into the record". The option asking for a story a week later without any words inserted erases precisely the variable that produces the effect.

qs.why: The subject of the previous clause is “the initial interview matters more than the tenth”, and “it” continues that subject; the rest of the sentence, “neutral in wording and free of hints”, can only apply to the interview.
qs.whyOthersFail: The wording option makes sense because the text indeed questions the verb "smashed", but if "it" means wording, the phrase "neutral in wording" in the same sentence becomes redundant. The tenth-interview option is equally plausible as court-recorded data, but the text uses "the tenth" precisely as a less important comparison within "the initial interview matters more than the tenth". The witness-belief option is also commonly recorded by courts, but the subsequent sentence forbids treating belief as evidence, rather than telling to record it.

qs.why: Ini parafrasa langsung: saksi bisa jujur dan keliru sekaligus.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the text states the same thing; "Not stated" is wrong because the sentence is in the final paragraph.

qs.why: The first paragraph states that procrastination follows emotions much more closely than it follows effort.
qs.whyOthersFail: The relief-training-habit option is the mechanism in paragraph two explaining that claim; the gentle-step option is its practical consequence in paragraph three; the demanding-standard option is the opening observation used to discard the word lazy.

qs.why: What is reported is a small rise in anxiety, boredom, or embarrassment when files are opened.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of losing interest throughout the afternoon turns a momentary feeling into a long-term state, whereas the text mentions “a modest surge” exactly when the file is opened. The option of wanting to plan first sounds like the procrastination we know, but the text does not report it; planning is instead discussed as failed advice. The option of being calm before the file is opened reverses the sequence, as relief only comes after the person switches to something else.

qs.why: The evidence is one study: forgiving previous procrastination is followed by less procrastination leading up to the exam.
qs.whyOthersFail: The two-minute task option is indeed a suggestion in the text, but no study results are attached to it, so it is not evidence. The strict list option reverses the text, which says a hard list actually increases pressure. The bad opening sentence option is also just practical advice; the text never compares its quality to a neat sentence.

qs.why: All four options use the same form, namely the basis of evidence followed by its consequence; the first warning mentions the study almost entirely involves students and relies on self-report, so the effect may be weaker in warehouses or wards.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are as elegant as a key and each shifts exactly one element. The option of observing students shifts the method, whereas the text mentions "depend on self-report". The option of a larger effect off-campus shifts the direction of the hypothesis, because the text mentions "may prove weaker". The option of evidence from wards and warehouses shifts the source, because those two places are precisely the ones that have not been tested.

qs.why: The text says switching to something else immediately erases that feeling, and that relief is the reward; this claim is the opposite.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is wrong because the polarity is reversed; "Not stated" is wrong because that relief is stated explicitly.

qs.why: All four options mention the same work, namely presenting two positions; the text determines the form: "the two positions share a target and separate over the remedy", and the author concludes without choosing.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are coherent with the thesis of two close positions and each is wrong on one element. Deciding which is more robust is blocked by "Neither position is a mere slogan". Differing on the goal is blocked by the sentence stating both share a target and separate over the remedy. The distance being too small to change teaching is blocked by "A teacher who follows the psychologist will console more readily, while a teacher who follows the trainer will instruct more".

qs.why: The patch: praise for effort must be honest, because children quickly detect fake praise.
qs.whyOthersFail: The wait-until-finished option sounds like a reasonable classroom rule, but the psychologist does not mention the timing of praise. The option of discarding the word clever is part of the old advice he received, not a patch he added. The option of calling that method the second researcher's position actually replaces effort with strategy, so the owner of the opinion is wrong.

qs.why: All four options mention it as a narrow difference; the text determines the consequence: a teacher who follows the psychologist will console more readily, while a teacher who follows the trainer will instruct more and perhaps console less.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options accept that the distance is narrow and the three distractors use the same "narrow but still" form as the key, so the form does not distinguish; what is wrong is the element. Separation on the goal is blocked by "the two positions share a target and separate over the remedy", because it is the remedy that separates. The word choice issue is blocked by "Neither position is a mere slogan". Already decided by the math trainer is blocked by "both survive contact with a noisy Monday class", because the author does not give victory to anyone.

qs.why: He says warm comments about trying “may reach the child as a polite verdict on her intelligence”, which is a subtle signal that expectations for the child are already low.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of protecting from intelligence praise makes sense because that is indeed the official reason for the advice to praise effort, but the trainer "doubts that effort is the appropriate replacement", so he does not use that defense. The option of already having a method sounds reasonable, but the text says "Effort combined with a poor method is merely exhausting" and what he praises is the choice of strategy, not the effort. The option of students struggling with math is very believable for a math teacher trainer, but the text never mentions any group of students as an exception.

qs.why: The text only mentions both were asked to give advice; the basis for that advice, let alone joint research, is never mentioned.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" requires joint research attribution that does not exist; "False" is also wrong because the text does not deny such a study, it is just silent.

qs.why: The closing sentence chooses a panel difficult to see behind glass with a written history and its claimant named, rather than a neat gallery that learns to say nothing.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of withdrawal protecting the institution is an observation from paragraph two that supports; the option of labels noting uncertainty is a detail of his proposal in paragraph three; the option of objects that remain stored is a consequence in paragraph four, not a recommended position.

qs.why: Crates in a warehouse generate no research, complaints, or conversations with the community that created them.
qs.whyOthersFail: The researcher flow option sounds reasonable for a museum warehouse, but the text says crates in a warehouse “generates no research”. The legal note option adds a benefit that was never mentioned; what is mentioned as missing is the wall label, the only place the museum makes a public promise. The savings option twists the sentence about costs: the text uses the cheapness of silence to accuse, not to say the money moved to labels.

qs.why: Contohnya konkret: label bisa mencantumkan resimen, tahun, kebakaran, dan penanda tangan kuitansi.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three-short-lines option is indeed a detail from the text, but it is a description of comments skipped by visitors, not evidence that labels can contain uncomfortable facts. The option of labels also disappearing is actually a consequence of the object's withdrawal, so the direction is opposite to the stem. The option of labels being rewritten whenever there is a claim adds a procedure that does not exist; the text only says labels can note who requested it and when.

qs.why: The text says objects removed quietly “tend to stay removed, since the pressure to act fades once the case stands empty”; that fading pressure is the point.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of steps toward return is a reasonable and widely held hope, but the text concludes: "Objects removed quietly tend to stay removed".
