qs.why: The author states that nothing in his writing should delay a successful claim; this claim is a paraphrase of that.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the content is in line; "Not stated" is wrong because the sentence is explicit in the final paragraph.

qs.why: All four options mention the same magnitude; the text determines the content: "the priority is not obvious, and it is not the statue", then the damp room is told to be handled first.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are in line with the thesis that paper is more fragile than bronze and each is wrong on one element. Dividing equally is blocked by the sentence that actually provides a ranking. Stopping the monument unveiling shifts the degree from delaying to forbidding and is blocked by "This is not a plea to demolish anything" and "Bronze survives a decade of delay without harm". Moving the deed to the capital shifts the location and is blocked by "The work also employs graduates in the town itself rather than a studio in the capital".

qs.why: What the archive needs is a dry cabinet with stable temperature, not ribbons and speeches.
qs.whyOthersFail: The ribbon and speech option is precisely what the text rejects: archives demand dry storage “rather than a ribbon”. The studio in the capital option reverses the sentence about labor, because that work is said to absorb graduates in the town itself. The boundary dispute option changes one example of ledger utility into a requirement before the archive is useful, whereas the text says archives answer questions not yet thought of.

qs.why: All four options acknowledge the civic value of the monument; the text determines the degree: the monument does teach civic sense, and the author still puts it in second place after the damp paper.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options give recognition then hold back in the same way, so the key register does not stand out; what is wrong is one of the elements. Slow to question costs is blocked by the cost sentence that is actually calculated, "listing and shelving an entire district collection costs less than one bronze figure". Considering neglect as a decision is blocked by "Neglect is rarely a decision; it is what happens when nobody decides". Handing the ranking to someone else is blocked by "the priority is not obvious, and it is not the statue".

qs.why: All four options use the same form; the text determines the content: a community that cannot produce its own documents ends up borrowing someone else's version, and that borrowed version is usually flattering.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are in the form of a paradox of a town without its own paper and each shifts one element. Borrowing the capital's ledger shifts the object from a version of the past to a document, and collides with work that is actually done in the town itself. Remembering the dispute shifts the scope to memory. A story that leaves no one behind reverses its direction, because "The borrowed version is usually a flattering one".

qs.why: The text mentions the cost is cheaper than one bronze statue, so this claim swaps the direction of the comparison.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is wrong because the numbers are reversed; "Not stated" is wrong because that cost comparison is indeed written.

qs.why: The text concludes with both answering separate questions and no source lying; each is asked things they never admitted to knowing.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of a genealogy that prunes generations is the habit of one source in paragraph two; the option of early tax records is the habit of another source in paragraph three; the option of pollen and wood is the way of reconciliation, not the central claim.

qs.why: What is missing from the count is a generation without disputes or migrations.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of names whose rights are disputed reverses the rule, because disputes are precisely what make a generation remembered. The option of ceremonies swaps the content of the list with the place where the list is recited. The option of spelling moves the problem from oral genealogy to colonial ledgers, two sources the text distinguishes carefully.

qs.why: The evidence: a hamlet is only recorded when there is a road, market, or dispute that draws it to the official's attention.
qs.whyOthersFail: The genealogy exercise option is evidence for the reliability of oral sources, not for the boundary of a ledger entry's meaning. The pollen and house wood option comes from the reconciliation paragraph and is actually used to mediate, not to evaluate early entries. The clerk's spelling option is indeed a weakness of the ledger, but it is a matter of swapped names, not whether early entries prove the founding of a village.

qs.why: The text says historians now treat that discrepancy “as evidence in itself rather than as an error requiring correction”, and the final paragraph shows what can be learned from it.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option that one of the records was reworked later is a reasonable conclusion from two clashing numbers, but the text asserts "Neither source was lying". The option of different hamlets using the spelling problem mentioned by the text, but the sentence itself says the ledger records "the same hamlet, under a slightly different spelling". The option of elders revising the count after hearing the ledger is just as plausible as an oral history process, but the correction mentioned by the text comes "in public by rivals", not from official documents.

qs.why: The text says a clerk's guess at a foreign sound can attach one hamlet's name to another hamlet's field, so this claim is a paraphrase, not a quote.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the claim content is in line with the text; "Not stated" is wrong because that spelling risk is discussed explicitly in the paragraph about ledgers.

qs.why: All four options mention the same work, namely contrasting two positions; the text determines the form: the distance is "narrower than it appears, and it is nonetheless real", and the choice is left as a matter of value.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three accept the thesis of two close positions and each is wrong on one element. Deciding which is more honest is blocked by "It is closer to a choice about which truth the terrace ought to carry", because the author does not choose. Differing on the wall engineering is blocked by "The second accepts the engineering and rejects the shape". Two different faculties is blocked by "trained in the same faculty".

qs.why: Menurut arsitek kedua, sambungan itu mengajari pengunjung bahwa masa lalu bisa dirapikan.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of weakening the wall sounds like a reasonable technical objection, but the text says he “accepts the engineering” and rejects the shape, not the strength. The option of being hidden under a canopy is off-target: the canopy is installed to stabilize the wall while letting the gap remain visible. The option of noting earthquakes reverses the role owner, because what he calls a document is the gap that is left, not a new mortar joint.

qs.why: All four options mention it as a small difference; the text determines the location: the distance is narrower than it appears and remains real, because one wants visitors to understand the building and one wants visitors to understand its history.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options accept the thesis that the two positions are close and the three distractors use the same concessive form as the key, so the form does not point to the key; what is wrong is the element. Can be closed by measurement is blocked by "committees dislike such choices, because measurement cannot settle them". The issue of invented ornament is blocked by "both refuse invented ornament", so that is not the axis of difference. Already decided by budget is blocked by "They agree on the danger and on the budget".

qs.why: All four options define ruins with the same elegance; the first architect calls it not a neutral state but a wound that keeps bleeding, because water enters, roots follow, and the surviving carvings fall last.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are in the form of equivalent definitions and each shifts one element. Ruins as a record shifts the agent to the second architect, "he sees a document which records the earthquake and the long neglect". A state that can withstand weather shifts the degree, whereas the wound is said to continue. Loss that has been limited by a catalog also shifts the degree, because stones cataloged in the field do not stop water and roots.

qs.why: The text only says both agree on the budget; the cost of a canopy compared to the cost of rebuilding is never compared.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" requires numbers that never appear; "False" is also wrong because the text does not deny it, it is just silent on that.

qs.why: All four options propose arguments with the same weight; the text determines the content: "The review therefore proposes a package rather than a designation", after explaining why designation without support fails.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are coherent with the thesis that owners need help, not just status, and each is wrong on one element. Listing alone is blocked by "Listing alone will not stop the decline" and the surge in demolition applications. Financing wood scarcity alone shifts the scope to one of three actions, whereas what is proposed is a package. Prioritizing the facade is blocked by "A repair scheme without records, meanwhile, will produce cheerful frontages over rotten frames".

qs.why: Of the 214 units surveyed, 61 still have original wooden frames, and 38 of them are heavily damaged.
qs.whyOthersFail: The 38 option swaps two text numbers: 38 is the part that is heavily damaged, not the one with original wooden frames. The 214 option uses the number of units surveyed as the number that still have original wood. The half-already-repaired option adds a repair claim that does not exist; the text actually says owners have difficulty getting wood and craftsmen.

qs.why: The evidence from the neighboring district: after listing without grants, demolition applications for safety reasons rose sharply.
qs.whyOthersFail: The scarcity of wood and tradespeople explains why owners are trapped, but that is not the result of unmonitored listings. The small-plot income option is used by the text to justify land levy deductions, not as evidence of a failed listing. The shortage of tradespeople is the reason for the apprenticeship proposal, and it remains valid with or without status designation.

qs.why: The condition was set precisely for that risk: grants can drive up property prices and accelerate tenant departures, “so the fund should be conditional on existing tenancies being renewed”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The inspection cost-cutting option makes sense because inspections are indeed mentioned, but inspections in the text are a way to disburse funds, not something saved by that condition. The receipt option is the most common grant condition in the real world, and that is precisely what the text rejects: funds are released "after inspection rather than on production of receipts". The option of filling the apprenticeship program is equally plausible, but the apprenticeship is a separate second proposal, whereas the condition in question is attached to the repair fund.

qs.why: Funds are indeed released after examination rather than after receipts are submitted; this claim matches.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the mechanism is the same; "Not stated" is wrong because the disbursement condition is written in the first proposal.

qs.why: The first paragraph states that what is debatable is the rise of a single magnitude—clicks—into a measure of editorial value without ever being announced.
qs.whyOthersFail: The reader data option that punctures comfort is the case of the defense party in paragraph three; the option of recording results is the proposal in paragraph four; the heavy and expensive subject option is the mechanism of its distortion in paragraph two.

qs.why: Within an hour, the article resulting from three weeks of work had already slumped below the tourist destination list.
qs.whyOthersFail: The withdrawn option because advertisers complained was blocked by the sentence that nothing was censored and no instruction to take it down was given. The rewritten option adds editorial desk interference that did not exist; what happened was merely that its ranking dropped. The longer reading time option reverses the result, because the article actually lost to the tourist destination list.

qs.why: All four options acknowledge the usefulness of reader data and then question a single matter; the text determines that matter: the difficulty lies not in measurement itself but in the selection of what gets measured.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options grant recognition first and then question a single matter, so their forms are uniform; each distractor targets the wrong object. Questioning the boredom punctured by data is blocked by "audience data punctures that comfort usefully", which the author actually acknowledges. Questioning the reporter's choice is blocked by "Nothing was censored and no instruction was issued", because it was the reporter who was disadvantaged. Questioning its old function as advertising space pricing is blocked by "The difficulty lies not in measurement itself but in the selection of what gets measured"; what is questioned is its current role, not its original usage.

qs.why: The reason is written explicitly: “Attention is cheap to quantify, whereas consequence is not”, and the canceled board decision “leaves no residue on any chart”; without the second column, such consequences count for nothing.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of publishing traffic numbers is a reasonable transparency proposal, but the inventory requested by the text is used within the newsroom and compared with explanations given to advertisers, not to readers. The option of being easier to sell to advertisers is equally commercially plausible, but the text states that the records are "considerably harder to explain to an advertiser". The option of pulling the screen sounds like a natural conclusion from this criticism, but the text opens with "Nobody in the trade would argue for less information".

qs.why: The text actually states that the shift never appeared in any meeting minutes, so the claim is reversed.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is wrong because it contradicts the sentence; "Not stated" is wrong because the matter of the minutes is indeed discussed.

qs.why: All four options present arguments as strong as a key; the text determines their substance: a prompt correction, "in the same position and at the same size as the original claim", is a verifiable promise.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three align with the thesis that trust is built by actions following an error, and each is wrong on a single element. Publishing an error-assessor policy shifts the scope, because that policy appears merely as a response to objections about a flood of complaints. Checking harder instead of correcting in front of readers is blocked by "There is a further gain, and it is internal", because that discipline is the result of a prominent correction, not its replacement. Readers forgiving after an explanation shifts the mechanism and is blocked by "What they monitor is the conduct which follows an error".

qs.why: Six lines at the bottom of the inner page, a few days later, in a font smaller than the advertisements.
qs.whyOthersFail: The front-page paragraph option is a state the author desires, not the habit he describes. The reader letters option adds a format never mentioned by the text. The position and size option is precisely the author's proposal in paragraph two, so it swaps an ideal for current practice.

qs.why: The evidence: a policy was published regarding what counts as an error and who decides to close trivial complaints.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option that readers have accepted the error answers another objection, namely whether mistakes damage trust. The option of superiority over competitors comes from the final paragraph regarding long-term benefits, not about handling complaints. The pre-publication checking option is an internal advantage that emerges after the policy is running, not the reason why complaints can be managed.

qs.why: All four options are written in the same two-way contrast; the concluding part determines the content: newspapers that hide their errors are asking to be trusted, whereas those that print them are providing reasons.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three share a two-way contrast format and each shifts a single element. Asking for patience and reaping praise shifts what is requested and obtained, because what is mentioned are trust and reasons to trust. Correcting versus repeating shifts its pairing, because the pair compared by the text is hiding versus printing. Hiding to protect the paper shifts the consequence and is blocked by "trust constructed on silence does not survive discovery".

qs.why: The author acknowledges that complaints aimed at exhausting the newsroom are real, and then states they can still be managed.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because the author acknowledges it; "Not stated" is wrong because the acknowledgment is clearly written.

qs.why: The first paragraph states that headlines can persist in memory long after the accompanying qualifications have grown stale.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of a more cautious headline remembered longer reverses the experiment's findings; the reader thoroughness option clashes with “Most people read the headline and nothing else”; the option of including every qualification clashes with headlines described as failing to attract anyone's attention.

qs.why: Seminggu kemudian dua kelompok itu mengingat versi tanpa pagar; kehati-hatiannya hilang.
qs.whyOthersFail: The cautious verb option is precisely what the text states “has largely disappeared” after a week. The base rate number option reverses the findings of paragraph three, because small numbers are what evaporate most often. The question format option uses one of the experimental treatments as the content of memory, whereas what remains is its flat statement.

qs.why: Relative changes are relatively easy to retain, whereas base figures are precisely what evaporate from memory.
qs.whyOthersFail: The identical body text option is experimental control regarding linguistic fences, not evidence about numbers. The many items each morning explain why people only read headlines, not why relative changes are stickier. The temporary findings option is a working rule in the final paragraph, making it a proposal rather than evidence.

qs.why: The sentence before that phrase gives the calculation: because explanatory details are inside the article, “it reaches fewer people than the assertion on the front”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The number of experiments option makes sense because the text does discuss research, but the phrase appears after a discussion of how many people reach each section, rather than how many times a study was repeated. The article length calculation option is equally plausible for the newsroom world, but the text never discusses article length. The two cases per ten thousand option uses figures that actually exist in the text, but those figures are the base rates forgotten by readers, not calculations about attention.

qs.why: The text discusses what readers remember, not whether fenced headlines make them check the study.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" and "False" both require causal explanations that are never written in the text.

qs.why: All four options mention the same work; the text determines its form: the gap is "narrower than the argument sounds, and it does not close", and the parting point is indicated without a winner.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are coherent with the thesis of two adjacent answers and each is wrong on a single element. Deciding which price is blocked by "The disagreement is therefore constitutional rather than commercial". Disagreeing on whether readers should pay is blocked by "They agree that the reader must now pay". A gap bridgeable by calculation is blocked by "no accounting exercise will resolve that".

qs.why: The first editor proposes a meter: five articles per month, after which it becomes paid.
qs.whyOthersFail: The donor-funded free access option clashes with their agreement that readers must start paying. The option of charging advertisers is rejected by both editors, who equally refuse advertisers dictating coverage. The annual membership option is the second editor's proposal, making it the wrong opinion holder.

qs.why: The reason is concrete: locked urban planning decision news is precisely what city residents need most.
qs.whyOthersFail: The occasional reader option is the first editor's argument about the meter, not the second editor's reason. The more easily forecast revenue option is actually refuted by the person himself, who acknowledges that membership revenue is “harder to forecast”. The option of advertisers dictating coverage is rejected by both in the concluding paragraph.

qs.why: The pointing sentence is clear: “The choice determines who remains outside, and no accounting exercise will resolve that”, so what is at stake is who is left outside.
qs.whyOthersFail: The advertiser versus reader option is the most common way to divide the media funding debate, but the text states "They agree that the reader must now pay". The reporter headcount option is equally plausible as a practical differentiator, but the difference in revenue projections is said not to trouble the second editor, and "no accounting exercise will resolve" the choice. The question of whether to keep printing is a real question for any weekly, but the text never touches upon print format.

qs.why: He himself admits that membership model revenue is harder to forecast, so this claim is inverted.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is wrong because it contradicts; "Not stated" is wrong because the revenue forecast matter is mentioned.

qs.why: All four options provide recommendations as strong as a key; the text determines their substance: "The proposal here separates the money from the decision", and it is detailed as a trusteeship where the assembly constitutes only a minority on the board.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three align with the thesis that the empty press bench must be funded, and each is wrong on a single element. Annual grants are blocked by "A newspaper whose budget is renewed each year by the body it exists to scrutinise will, in time, scrutinise it more gently". Handing financing to the broadcaster shifts control, because broadcasters merely pay license fees whereas the board of trustees decides. Delaying the decision is blocked by "Neither risk is a reason to leave the press bench empty" and a decision already twice postponed.

qs.why: The governing board is designed so that assembly seats remain a minority.
qs.whyOthersFail: The editors option mixes two things: editors hold editorial control, not trusteeship governance. The assembly committee option reverses the design, because the assembly was intentionally placed as a minority. The regional broadcaster option uses the fee-paying party as the governing party, whereas the text only mentions the source of funds.

qs.why: Experience from other regions: once grants are given per department, coverage of that department thins within two years.
qs.whyOthersFail: The nineteen boards option measures the scale of coverage vacuums, not the result of direct grants. The one journalist for two papers option is also a collapse statistic, not evidence regarding grants. The evaluation criteria option is a new proposal design, so it comes after the objection, not supporting that objection.

qs.why: The condition was set for the explicitly named risk: “the first is displacement: a title given a funded reporter may simply cut a post of its own”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of increasing the number of trials covered makes sense because the text does use trial counts as an evaluation criterion, but that criterion is for selecting recipients, not a staffing condition. The minority assembly seats option is a safeguard genuinely present in the text, but that is the answer to the second risk, namely board capture. The option of lowering license fees is equally plausible as a policy motive, but the text only mentions that the fees are small and does not connect them to any condition.

qs.why: Kendali redaksi disebut tetap sepenuhnya di tangan editor penerima reporter itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is wrong because it aligns with the text; "Not stated" is wrong because editorial control is stated explicitly.

qs.why: A coastal city that diverted heavy transport recorded one-fifth fewer child hospital admissions with zero hospital spending; traffic orders accomplished it.
qs.whyOthersFail: Hospital admissions booked as treatments is an accounting convention in paragraph one; the two separate books option is the answer to the objection in paragraph three; publishing figures per road is the proposal in paragraph four.

qs.why: The city diverted heavy transport from three residential streets, and then child admissions dropped by a fifth.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of building an emergency room clashes with “Nothing was spent on hospitals”. The option of replacing the entire bus fleet uses cost examples from paragraph three, not actions taken by that coastal city. Publishing figures per road is the author's proposal in the final paragraph, not what the city has already done.

qs.why: All four options acknowledge real costs; the text determines the next step: financial objections deserve an answer, transport diversion costs are acknowledged, and the comparison offered is almost always called wrong.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options acknowledge costs first, so the concede-then-withhold form no longer marks the key; what is wrong is the element. Doubting the intentions of transport entrepreneurs is blocked by "Objections are usually financial, and they deserve an answer". Telling transport authorities to bear it is blocked by the actual proposals, "no accountant is asked to add the two columns together" and "publish one figure alongside the other". Making costs the determinant is blocked by "the comparison offered is almost always the wrong one".

qs.why: Kalimatnya menyebut ketidaknyamanannya dan sebabnya: “because it identifies the streets that have been neglected”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of lowering admission numbers makes sense because the text does have examples of drops, but what lowered them were traffic rules, whereas publishing figures only makes prevention visible. The option of claiming savings is a reasonable administrative exit, but the text actually states "no accountant is asked to add the two columns together". The state-of-the-art monitor option is equally believable as a consequence of transparency, but monitor readings in the text are used to pair figures with roads, not to rank tools.

qs.why: Clinical savings go to the health department, while traffic regulation costs are paid by the transportation department.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is incorrect because that is exactly what it says; "Not stated" is incorrect because the budget allocation is written.

qs.why: The concluding paragraph mentions that the technique is not a substitute for clinical reporting and is better understood as an early warning.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of the signal rising earlier is its time advantage in paragraph two; the rain and industry options are its limitations in paragraph three; the one-week option that is only useful for districts ready to act is a condition of its use, not a primary assessment of the method.

qs.why: The figure is four to seven days before reported cases begin to rise.
qs.whyOthersFail: The one-to-two-day option shrinks the gap that the text calls four to seven days. The two-week option enlarges it, even though the text only says “A week is a considerable interval”. The same-day option removes its time advantage, which is precisely cited as the main benefit of this method.

qs.why: The chain is detailed: "clinical figures depend on a sequence of decisions: somebody must feel unwell, decide to seek advice, obtain a test and have the result registered". All four steps must be complete before a single case appears in clinical figures.
qs.whyOthersFail: The sewage sampling sequence is not a clinical figure chain, and "Sewage skips the sequence entirely" blocks options that include rainwater dilution within it. The option that places the sewage signal rise first and then clinics confirm who is affected REVERSES the direction and exceeds the evidence: "It cannot say by whom". Reminding clinicians what to look for is a RESPONSE after a warning ("by opening testing sites or reminding clinicians what to look for"), not a prerequisite before someone decides to seek help.

qs.why: The sentence is straightforward: without the capacity to act, sampling “merely documents an epidemic that arrives on schedule”; the data exists, the prevention does not.
qs.whyOthersFail: The factory waste sample option is flawed because it uses a limitation actually mentioned in the text, but that limitation applies generally and is not specific to districts without capacity. The faster clinical figures option is equally plausible for areas with organized clinics, but the text states the water channel signal appears "between four and seven days before reported cases began to climb". The option to add sampling points is a reasonable technical suggestion, but the text concludes with "The instrument is cheap; the response is the expensive part".

qs.why: The text explicitly states that the signal cannot tell how severely people are affected.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" is incorrect because it reverses the content of the sentence; "Not stated" is incorrect because the limitations are explicitly mentioned.

qs.why: The text mentions that a sensible program uses both instruments without pretending both are equal in reach.
qs.whyOthersFail: The labeling option that shifts shoppers who were already careful is a finding in paragraph two; the reformulation option that lowers intake is a finding in paragraph three; the official who likes disclosure is a concluding accusation, not an assessment of both.

qs.why: The shift is small and concentrated among shoppers who were already paying attention to package contents from the start.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option that it changes nothing is too strong, because the text acknowledges labels “do shift purchasing”, albeit slightly. The option that it is most effective for the heaviest salt eaters reverses the findings: they are actually the ones who change the least. The fifteen percent reduction option moves the results of the reformulation program to the label.

qs.why: The mechanism is two consecutive sentences: "Because the reduction falls below the threshold of detection, the taste of any single loaf does not appear to change. Preference itself adjusts downwards over several years, which is why the strategy compounds." Small annual reductions are undetectable, then taste adjusts downward so the effect compounds.
qs.whyOthersFail: One large cut in a single season conflicts with the core requirements of "a few per cent a year" and "below the threshold of detection". Reading warnings on packaging and then switching products is ANOTHER instrument (labeling); the text asserts reformulation "requires no participation from the shopper". Linking the cuts to categories where sales have already fallen INVENTS a condition that is actually refuted by the text: "Sales in the categories involved showed no measurable decline."

qs.why: All four options use the same two-way contrast; the text determines the content: information rewards people who were already reading, whereas those with the highest intake changed the least.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are equal in form and each shifts one element. Reaching the most users reverses the target and is blocked by "Those consuming the most salt tend to change the least". Lowering the level added by producers shifts the agent to reformulation. Shifting every shopper slightly shifts the coverage, because the shift is "concentrated among shoppers who were already attentive".

qs.why: The text only says producers agreed to reduce levels; the matter of tax incentives is not mentioned at all.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" and "False" both demand information about taxes that never appeared in the text.

qs.why: All four options mention the same work; the text determines the form: the difference regarding where efforts are focused is "worth setting out", because the budget is only enough for one.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three are coherent with the thesis of one budget for two plans and each is wrong on one element. Deciding which is wiser is blocked by "It looks like a judgement about who the campaign is for". Differing on breeding grounds is blocked by "Both accept that the mosquito breeds in domestic water containers". Showing the choice is technical is blocked by "the choice looks less like a technical question".

qs.why: The steps are sequential in one sentence: "Volunteers visit each compound, empty the containers, cover the tanks and return a fortnight later to check." The follow-up visit two weeks later is a fixed part of the first officer's plan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Weekly larval monitoring at fixed points with a threshold is the SECOND officer's plan, not the first. Street fogging is directly blocked by "Neither would spend the money on fogging the streets". A single visit removes the re-examination step and EXAGGERATES the text's claim: the text only mentions that people shown larvae "behave differently afterwards", not that the second visit becomes unnecessary.

qs.why: The reason: areas with the highest transmission are actually empty during working hours, so volunteer visits are missed.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of killing adult mosquitoes is the reason the first officer rejected spraying, not the reason for the second officer. The option of residents seeing larvae is also the first officer's argument regarding participation. The option of breeding grounds is a premise both agree on, so it cannot support one side.

qs.why: The text mentions the difference as a choice about which failure is more acceptable, then concludes “It looks like a judgement about who the campaign is for”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option regarding how mosquitoes breed is plausible as the root of the technical dispute, but the text says "Both accept that the mosquito breeds in domestic water containers". The option of the budget portion for fogging is equally reasonable in any health department meeting, but both rejected fogging from the start. The option of the frequency of issuing a larval index sounds like a debatable detail, but the text mentions both agreed to issue it per neighborhood.

qs.why: Keduanya sepakat menerbitkan indeks larva per lingkungan, jadi klaim ini parafrasa langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" is incorrect because the agreement is written; "Not stated" is incorrect because it is mentioned in the final paragraph.

qs.why: All four options propose changes of the same magnitude; the text determines the content: what is proposed is a threshold, not a consideration, and four actions take effect automatically once the threshold is exceeded.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three align with the thesis that the ten hottest days must be handled earlier, and each is wrong on one element. Ordering departments to move faster maintains official discretion and is blocked by "Discretion, in an emergency of this kind, functions as delay". Building refrigerated rooms is blocked by "None of the four requires new construction". Fixing the list of vulnerable residents shifts the coverage, because that list is noted as a weakness of the plan, not as a proposal.

qs.why: Excess deaths are concentrated among residents over seventy who live alone on upper floors.
qs.whyOthersFail: The field worker option uses one of the response steps (working hours shifted to the morning) as the most at-risk group. The option of three wards with the most shade reverses the pattern, because those at risk are wards with the least tree cover. The option of passengers at transport hubs takes the location of water points, not the group whose data shows excess deaths.

qs.why: The trigger is a threshold, not a person's judgment: "When the forecast night-time minimum exceeds a stated figure for two consecutive nights, four measures take effect automatically."
qs.whyOthersFail: A manager's decision is the OLD arrangement that is to be replaced: "Response at present depends on the discretion of individual departments." Waiting for two days of rising hospital admissions REVERSES the plan's intent, because that delay is what is being corrected: "action begins on the second or third day of a heat episode, by which time admissions have already risen". Updating the list of vulnerable residents is mentioned as an acknowledged weakness, not a prerequisite: "Neither weakness argues against the threshold."

qs.why: One sentence contains both: planting “will not affect this year or the next, though it remains the only measure that reduces the underlying hazard”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option as an alternative is plausible because both are about heat, but the text says both weaknesses "argue for beginning the slower work at the same time", so it is not a choice of one or the other. The cheapest option sounds reasonable for tree planting, but the text never compares the costs of the four actions. The option of including four automatic actions is also believable, but the four are mentioned one by one and planting is not on that list.

qs.why: The text states that none of the four steps require new construction, only earlier decisions.

qs.why: The concluding clause mentions that the diagnosis turned the feeling of humiliation into data, so the taste referred to is a taste for information about one's own mistakes, not the common meaning of the word in the mouth.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options use the same “Once …” structure and are equally precise. The option of a less sensitive mouth uses the literal meaning of “palate”, whereas this sentence uses a metaphor for a taste for information about difficulty. The option of hearing what a competent musician does uses the paragraph one phrase about acceleration, not this metaphor. The option of correction that is no longer painful deletes the active part, which is the taste that must be developed first.

qs.why: The text mentions her age and mentions the reason felt administrative, but the actual cause is never detailed.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” adds a cause not in the text, and “False” is also wrong because no sentence refutes it.

qs.why: The sentence gives the role of recording to the collection and leaves the mechanical work to the author, then the following sentence adds that preferences appear statistically, in repetition.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of her choosing reverses “The collection registers what I return to, and I merely operate the pen”; the option of the book recording her days conflicts with the opening sentence, “The notebook is not a diary”; the option of intending to record her own taste conflicts with “assembled without a system” and with preferences that appear statistically.

qs.why: The previous sentence mentions the habit of carrying other people's sentence containers turns ordinary hearing into a kind of harvesting, and this sentence is the example.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are equally straightforward and consistent with the thesis that collecting changes the collector. The option of being more attentive to friends reverses the value of her admission, as the following sentence calls it “a shabby discovery”. The option of friends who know is never mentioned by the text. The option of avoiding certain conversations conflicts with the clause “the noticing continues regardless”.

qs.why: Two signs are placed side by side: the word “shabby” for the discovery, and the admission of having no defense whatsoever.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of feeling happy conflicts with the word “shabby”; the option of not harming anyone actually provides a defense that the clause “I possess no defence” rejects, and conflicts with “not entirely benign”; the option of being distant conflicts with the phrase “about oneself”, which places the discovery on herself.

qs.why: The sentence rejects one comparison and then sets up a replacement: not a database, but an unhurried companion with its own opinions.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of a database is exactly what the sentence rejects, “not a database but an unhurried companion”; the option of asserting her writing intention conflicts with “dismantles the paragraph I had intended”; the option of getting along better reverses the words “arguing with my intentions”.

qs.why: The text asserts it is not a diary, so this claim directly contradicts its first sentence.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” conflicts with the words “not a diary”, and “Not stated” fails because the difference is explicitly explained.

qs.why: The sentence names the pattern of her entire essay, and paragraph three closes by calling the remaining count a loving part, expressed in the notation she trusts most.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options use the same “X rather than Y” structure, so the form does not point to the key. The option of letters as evidence is the stance of paragraph four regarding how they are kept. The option of capital letters is the explanation in paragraph one about her writing habit. The option of her own handwriting is the closing line summarizing her legacy, whereas the question asks what she finally understood from the letters, “Emotional information … travelled disguised as household maintenance”.

qs.why: The sentence sets up two things at once: the material had been there for two decades, and the reading only came from her sister.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of an unsupported explanation conflicts with the count that is indeed in every letter; the option of a count newly added in the final year conflicts with “Every missive harbours a minute calculation”; the option of half-understanding beforehand conflicts with “It required my sister to decode what had been present for two decades”.

qs.why: The sentence explains the full signature as a rejection of doubt about who is speaking, and the following sentence calls it a small, daily rejection.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of becoming funnier conflicts with “now legible as something else entirely”; the option of formerly moving swaps her initial assessment, which the text calls “formerly comic”; the option of administrative fussiness misses the reason given by the next sentence, which is the rejection of ambiguity about who is speaking.

qs.why: The word “purchased” sets up her father as the payer and the author's negligence as the item bought, then the concluding clause adds that the arrangement was never disclosed.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of the father never being corrected conflicts with “relentless correction at school”; the option of an arrangement explained to the family conflicts with “without once disclosing the arrangement to anybody”; the option of paying for her own education reverses the direction of the money, as the surplus was sent to her children.

qs.why: The reason for the capital letters reached her through her aunt, so this claim is an accurate paraphrase.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” contradicts the sentence, and “Not stated” fails because the source of the information is mentioned.

qs.why: The key sentence states that trust collapses not because the science is wrong, but because it is sold with excessive certainty. What is sold with excessive certainty is a single number without its range, and that is the essence of this key.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors accept the thesis that over-certainty damages trust, but they miss the target or the degree. The newspaper error option is refuted by “it descends upon the sciences rather than upon the newspapers that shorten them”; the self-protection through qualification option is refuted by “the scientist sheltering behind qualifications fails in the contrary direction”; the reader-training option is refuted by “Audiences, however, are not infants”.

qs.why: The reason provided by the text for editors is only about the format that fits into colored panels, and the next paragraph states that readers do pay a high price for certainty. Thus, editors are serving a demand, not inventing numbers.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of belittling readers clashes with “Audiences, however, are not infants” and the reason provided, which is market demand; the option of moving ranges to the body of the news clashes with “the brackets are silently deleted”; the option of viewing ranges as avoiding decisions is the reaction of listeners and funding agencies, not the editors.

qs.why: The paragraph discusses doubt using commercial language: expensive to articulate, cheap to disregard, thin market. That is dry irony, not anger.
qs.whyOthersFail: The neutral option clashes with the clear judgment in “expensive to articulate and cheap to disregard”; the option of excusing the editor shifts the Friday deadline, which in that paragraph belongs to the committee, not the editor; the option of being furious on behalf of researchers exceeds the tone of the paragraph, which describes incentives bitterly rather than defending a party.

qs.why: The sentence directly equates the brackets with a confidence interval, which is how far a result might shift if the study were repeated. Thus, it refers to the numerical range, not the punctuation marks.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors are definitions that are equally precise for other meanings of the word, and each is refuted by one cue. The punctuation mark option and the tax bracket layer option fail because the sentence pairs the word with “a confidence interval registers how far a measurement might wander”; the difference between two measurements option fails because of the qualifying phrase “were the same study repeated”, which means the same measurement is repeated, not compared to another.

qs.why: The text says that what reaches the public is only one number, detached from the brackets that previously accompanied it. The claim is just a change in wording, the content is the same, so it is True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” requires a text that states the opposite, and that does not exist. “Not stated” also fails because the sentence explicitly mentions a single number without its range.

qs.why: The text says the workshop is where tools and techniques truly accumulate, while theology has long imagined history as a single narrative with a destination. Once both are combined, that uphill hybrid emerges.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options use the same two-way structure, so elegance does not mark the key. The reversed role option fails because it was theology that “had long conceived history as a single narrative possessing a destination”; the removed milestone option fails because the hybrid is actually “furnished with measurable milestones”; the separate measurement option fails because of the word “hybrid” in the same sentence.

qs.why: If a word feels natural, it is a word that has stopped being examined, and that is precisely where examination is most needed. The text says the difference is most important exactly when the vocabulary still feels natural.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors use the same inversion as the key, so the form no longer reveals the answer. The option of steadfastness disqualifying evidence is refuted by “treat such vocabulary as evidence rather than as neutral instruments”; the option of losing power after being tracked adds consequences not stated, as the reason promised by the text is only that it “exposes that verdict to inspection”; the option of no verdict is refuted by “The term had thereby become an argument, although it continued to resemble a mere description”.

qs.why: The phrase “conveniently justified whatever they were already undertaking” is an accusation of self-interest, but the author still admits the hybrid is “extremely convenient” and useful. Thus, it is measured suspicion.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors agree that the 19th-century usage was self-interested, but they are wrong in degree or target. The deliberate deception option is too harsh, as the text admits the tools “genuinely did accumulate” and calls the power of the keyword “hushed”; the option of blaming the craftsman misses the target because the author is questioning those who use that path, not the workshop; the tendency to agree option is refuted by “the arrangement conveniently justified whatever they were already undertaking”.

qs.why: The final paragraph acknowledges real improvements, then questions the step from many individual improvements to a single upward line that everyone must follow. That is the essence of this key.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are in the same two-way contrast form, and each distractor shifts exactly one element of the source claim. The inevitable path option shifts the degree and is refuted by “That line was drawn by particular individuals for particular purposes, and it can be redrawn”; the doubted improvement option shifts a claim that is actually acknowledged, “Water supplies improve, techniques sharpen”; the real incline and borrowed improvement option reverses the direction of the acknowledgment.

qs.why: The text says that in the 17th century, the word still meant a literal journey, and the meaning of rising-up came later. The claim is a direct opposite, hence False.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” would clash with the sentence about the royal procession. “Not stated” is also wrong because the chronology is explicitly mentioned.

qs.why: The author acknowledges that everyone knows the encore is coming, then says the cynics' objection wrongly equates ritual with deception. Thus, it is precisely the openly staged nature that makes the encore work.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors agree that what works is its open stage nature, but one element is shifted. The option of the audience forgetting is refuted by “Everyone in the auditorium is aware it is imminent”; the printed program option and the paid debt option each take one supporting reason opened by “Part of the explanation resides in” and make it the entire value, whereas it is the cynical objection that is answered by “this objection confuses ritual with outright deception”.

qs.why: Two hours of sitting silently, obediently, and almost invisibly is a passive position, and the text says the encore “inverts that arrangement briefly” because the audience's noise brings out the music.
qs.whyOthersFail: The heavier discipline on the audience side fails because the text also attaches discipline to the players: the audience “has learnt its part” and the players' astonishment is called “a rehearsed skill like any other”. The attention worth winning fails because the silence is described as a one-way transaction where no one speaks or is noticed. And the player's request fails because the applause is called “not a request but a cue” that comes from the audience.

qs.why: Penulis bilang para sinis “are not mistaken” soal faktanya, lalu bilang keberatan itu “confuses ritual with outright deception”. Faktanya diterima, simpulannya ditolak.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are in the form of “acknowledging the fact while …”, so the form does not mark the key; each distractor shifts one step. The option of narrowing the claim itself is refuted by “this objection confuses ritual with outright deception”, which rejects the conclusion instead of minimizing the claim; the option of blaming taste swaps the target, because what is refuted is the conclusion; the untrained astonishment option is refuted by “a rehearsed skill like any other”.

qs.why: The previous sentence says the concert is “a formal object, timed and published, and its architecture must be honoured from the opening note”. Thus, it refers to the fixed program, not the building.
qs.whyOthersFail: The building design option uses the most common meaning of “architecture”, whereas this sentence calls it “a formal object, timed and published”; the difficulty level sequence option adds a pattern not mentioned; the applause pattern option is an audience cue in paragraph one, not the formal form of that night.

qs.why: The text says the applause is not a request but a cue that comes at the right time. The claim is the same, just using different words, so it is True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” needs a text that says the applause is a real request, and that is precisely what is refuted. “Not stated” fails because the sentence is explicit.

qs.why: The key sentence says no one planned anything there, but the place has a clear order, and that order is written by use rather than by drawing. Thus, the absence of a plan is precisely the requirement.
qs.whyOthersFail: The author's interpretation option clashes with “it possesses an unmistakable order”, which is stated as a finding, not a reading; the origin from a survey option clashes with “inscribed by use rather than by drawing”; the old plan remnant option adds a history that does not exist.

qs.why: The author has said the value of the place lies precisely in the absence of function, and function is something always brought in by planning. Thus, the notification ensures that the value will disappear.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors use the same sign as the key, which is a rejection of entertainment in the form of “X, which is actually not Y”, but the content is wrong. The option of a guardian for the land has the wrong object because what is valued is the lack of function, “Its value consists precisely in its lack of function”; the hated tree option is refuted by “Three mature trees are preferable to none”; the option of people who stay is refuted by the closing sentence, “will migrate to some further gap that the plan has not yet registered”.

qs.why: The author writes “I minded considerably more than I could justify to anybody who enquired”. That is annoyance that is acknowledged yet cannot be defended, a semi-embarrassed regret.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options now open with the same word, so the form does not mark the key, and what distinguishes them are the degree and the target. The option of a defensible objection and the open anger option are refuted by the same phrase, “I minded considerably more than I could justify to anybody who enquired”; the option of regretting the crate and bramble has the wrong object, because what is valued is the lack of function and the author actually refuses to call the place attractive.

qs.why: The text explains the term: a residual space is whatever the design drawings cannot absorb, and every scheme produces some of it “however meticulous the planner has been”. The key states this in other words.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options use the same contrastive form, so the key is not unique in its elegance, and each distractor shifts exactly one element. The negligent planner option is refuted by “however meticulous the planner has been”; the intentionally set-aside space option is refuted by “whatever the drawings could not absorb”; the option about land that is actually listed moves “an unshaded interval between two numbered plots” from paragraph one to the definition of the term.

qs.why: The text mentions two different time markers: eleven years is how long he has been walking past, while the habit of pausing only began recently (“recently I began pausing there”). Thus, the claim that he routinely paused throughout the eleven years is contradicted by the text, not just unmentioned, so the key is False.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” only works if you equate two time markers that the author intentionally separates: walking past for eleven years vs. beginning to pause recently. “Not stated” also fails because the text is not silent on this: the words “recently I began” explicitly place the pausing habit at the end of the eleven-year span, so the duration is refuted, not left blank.

qs.why: The objectors consider the thicket a sign of neglect; the advocates sell photos of open fields. Both are about appearance, and the text says the parish council's objection “is rarely about biodiversity at all”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The second objection option that answers the first conflicts with the sentence “Advocates entertain their own version of the same confusion”, which places both at the same root; the species count option conflicts with “will not be answered by a further leaflet crowded with species counts”; the grazing cost option adds a topic not discussed.

qs.why: The text says selling an image of open emptiness will result in visitors who feel cheated by the thicket that ecology genuinely requires, and the sixth year is exactly when the thicket is dense.
qs.whyOthersFail: All three distractors use the same sign of disappointment as the key, so the register no longer marks it, but each has the wrong object. The muddy path option is refuted by “visitors who feel cheated by the thicket that ecology genuinely requires”; the explanatory leaflet option is refuted by “it will not be answered by a further leaflet crowded with species counts”; the option blaming the ecology is refuted by “A promise made in pictures will be judged in pictures”.

qs.why: The text calls this “a case against the vocabulary of stepping back, which promises humility and delivers an unexamined preference”. Thus, the phrase is accused of disguising a decision as restraint.
qs.whyOthersFail: The praise option fails because the phrase is said to promise humility but delivers an unexamined preference. The harmless brochure language option fails because the text draws its entire problem from that very vocabulary. And the cautious attitude regarding varying results fails because the choice is formulated as “visible management” versus management made to look like nature.

qs.why: The word “Visually” in front places that sentence in the realm of visual interpretation: a thicket that is ecologically good is still read as neglect.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are equally firm definitions and equally precise, three of which are for other meanings of the word. The option about reading a notice board and the option about numbers on a measuring tool fail because the sentence reads “Visually it reads as neglect”, which is how people's eyes interpret things, not tracing writing or scales; the land condition option moves the word to an inference from rain, whereas the subject is the thicket being viewed.

qs.why: The text says the thorny thicket appeared within four years after the fence was removed. The twenty-year claim swaps the numbers, so it is a direct contradiction, i.e., False.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” clashes with the four-year figure in the text. “Not stated” is wrong because the timeframe is explicitly mentioned.

qs.why: The key sentence says the methodological error is not exploring, but presenting exploration as if it were confirmation. This key states the same thing using different words.
qs.whyOthersFail: The “failed replication” vocabulary fails because the text places it as an opener regarding reputation, while the words “The methodological error” are placed elsewhere. The sampling variation option fails because the text only says that variation guarantees “some proportion” of studies differ, not the majority. And the boredom option fails because the text leaves it hanging: “whether that trade is acceptable depends upon what a particular field most urgently lacks”.

qs.why: The text says each decision is defensible in isolation, but their combination can produce convincing results from mere noise. Thus, false results can emerge without the intent to deceive.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option about being caught by reviewers adds oversight not discussed in that paragraph; the option about removing participants for inappropriate reasons conflicts with “Each decision is defensible in isolation”; the option about realizing the combined effect while choosing conflicts with the reason that makes pre-registration necessary, which is the flexibility remaining after data arrives.

qs.why: The result of the reform is called “instructive rather than triumphant”, then the gains and costs are placed side by side. That is qualified approval.
qs.whyOthersFail: The bitter regret option only takes half the scale and ignores “Registered studies report smaller effects” as an achievement; the impatience with critics option conflicts with “which is plausible”, which actually grants them part of the truth; the skeptical option regarding the reform's impact conflicts with “The reform has been widely adopted”.

qs.why: The text says the question worth asking is not whether the results are significant, but whether anyone has yet attempted to reproduce it and with what results. That is the content of this key.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option about asking for registration uses the topic of paragraph two, while the reader's advice reads “whether anybody has yet attempted to reproduce it”; the removed participant option is also from paragraph two; the large laboratory option adds criteria never mentioned by the text.

qs.why: The text says registered studies more often report smaller effects and null findings. The claim changes the words to “modest or empty”, the content is identical, so True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” requires an opposing statement that is not in the text. “Not stated” is wrong because that comparison is explicitly mentioned.

qs.why: The author says that four-bar section is not the goal, but a tool to build a kind of attention that will wait for the next bars. So the actual result is the ability to observe.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option about repetition that finally succeeds conflicts with “on Thursday the seam reopened without warning” and with “repetition merely reinforces whatever the hand is already performing”; the longer practice session option conflicts with the same sentence; the option about mastery that feels empty is an observation from paragraph four, not the main point.

qs.why: The text says that observation does not come from effort but from attention, and attention is called a completely different ability. So hard work is not automatically the same as observing accurately.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option about desire sharpening attention conflicts directly with “Attention, unlike effort, cannot be increased by wanting it more”; the number of hours option conflicts with the rejection of repetition in paragraph two; the option about errors stopping after being found conflicts with the seam opening again on Thursday.

qs.why: The word “restful” is placed after a contrast with a coworker whose response depends on everything except precision. That is a sense of relief.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options mention the same sense of relief, so what must be read is the reason. The option about effort being valued is refuted by “It responds to precisely one variable, which is whether the thumb releases at the appropriate instant”; the annoyance option is refuted by the word the author uses himself, “Such indifference is restful”; the regret option because no one witnessed it moves “humiliating in a manner no audience ever witnesses” from paragraph two to this sentence.

qs.why: The word is used for the connection of the hand transfer which, if done correctly, cannot be heard. The teacher uses that term for that vulnerable point.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are equally concise definitions and equally precise. The fabric seam option is the most common dictionary meaning, refuted by its usage for “a migration of the left hand from one position to another”; the bow direction option is refuted by “the bow continues without interruption”; the gap on the instrument body adds damage to an object never mentioned.

qs.why: The text says the author considers those two successes accidental, not proof of progress. The claim reverses that attitude, so False.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” clashes with the word “accidental” in the same sentence. “Not stated” is wrong because the author's attitude regarding Tuesday is clearly stated.

qs.why: The text says senior staff retreated to floors with fewer visitors, while the transparency works hardest on those with the least authority.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are two-way relations of equal precision, so the key does not stand out. The senior option is refuted by “the transparency operates most severely upon those with the least authority”; the perfectly flat hierarchy option stops at the concession “in one narrow respect it genuinely is” and ignores the subsequent “But”; the even surveillance option is refuted by “Visibility, distributed unevenly”.

qs.why: Paragraph two provides the physical requirements: transparency needs a difference in light, and “by daylight the exterior is invariably brighter than the interior behind it”, so on a bright June afternoon, the facade becomes a mirror reflecting the sky, traffic, and the pedestrians themselves.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option about seeing the office behind it reverses that light requirement. The option about seeing nothing because the glass is dark is the wrong type: the text says the facade is not transparent but a mirror; something is visible, just not the interior. The option about one floor being faintly visible offers a middle ground not in the text, which writes “not transparent at all”, not partially.

qs.why: The phrase “heavily advertised” is placed right next to “cannot be exercised”. That sentence strikes at the gap between the promise and the result.
qs.whyOthersFail: The praise option fails because after dark the occupants have left and “virtually nobody is watching”. The neutral summary option fails because the word “heavily advertised” is already judgmental. And the admission that the promise is figurative fails because the text says openness is promised “as though it were a structural property of the cladding”, so it is demanded literally.

qs.why: The sentence sets up two parallel denials: a company does not become transparent just by installing glass walls, just as a person does not become honest just by opening curtains. The key restates both.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options use the same two-part structure and each distractor shifts exactly one element. The option about curtains keeping people honest maintains half the analogy that is actually being denied; the option about glass making concealment difficult is refuted by paragraph two, “by daylight the exterior is invariably brighter than the interior behind it”; the option about candor not needing to be maintained is refuted by “Candour is a practice, patiently maintained”.

qs.why: The text says the glass envelope surrenders heat in winter. The claim just changes “surrenders it in winter” to losing heat in the cold months, so it is True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” requires a statement that glass retains heat in winter, and that is not there. “Not stated” fails because its thermal behavior is mentioned directly.

qs.why: The author calls marginalia the most honest record we have of how people used to read, and says the practice reveals more about attention than borrowing numbers.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option about better Renaissance readers adds a quality comparison not made by the text; the aggregate highlighting option clashes with “volume has thereby replaced argument”; the option about library rules needing to be relaxed clashes with “librarians discourage it for entirely defensible reasons”.

qs.why: Buku murah disebut sekali pakai, dan barang sekali pakai nggak memancing komitmen. Jadi harga murah menurunkan rasa bahwa buku itu layak diperlakukan serius.
qs.whyOthersFail: The text says cheap books are disposable and disposable items do not invite commitment, so annotations decrease, not increase. Publishers are said to never encourage buyers to mark their merchandise. And libraries actually forbid the practice entirely.

qs.why: The author says the most frequently marked sentences might be the wisest or just the easiest to quote, then closes with “volume has thereby replaced argument”. That is a skeptical stance.
qs.whyOthersFail: The hopeful option and the curious option both stop at the concession “in certain respects it has” and miss the assessment “without reporting why” as well as “the aggregate has no temper”; the option about being annoyed at readers shifts the target of the objection from the aggregate to the person.

qs.why: The word is contrasted with “comment column”, and the context is about extracting and rearranging material. So the meaning is a place to work, not a place to judge.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options are definitions of equal precision, three of which are for other meanings of the word. The bookbinding room option uses the most literal meaning and is unrelated to margins; the short course option uses the second common meaning; the comment column option is exactly what the sentence rejects, “as a workshop rather than as a comment column”.

qs.why: The text only tells of one volume and one word that appears forty times in it. Whether that reader wrote the same word in other books is never touched upon, so it is Not stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” adds books that never existed in the text. “False” is also wrong because the text does not deny anything about that reader's collection; it is simply silent.

qs.why: The key sentence says the detection rate is a strong measure for change at one location over time, and a fragile measure for quantity at one moment. This key states both sides.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options open with the same claim, so the thesis guessed from other questions is not enough; the second clause must be read. The option about path bias as the deepest flaw elevates one of two difficulties into the core and is refuted by “None of this undermines the method”; the large archive option producing counts is refuted by “abundance must be inferred from a model rather than observed”; the option about comparisons across landscapes is refuted by “Comparisons across years, at identical stations, are therefore far safer than comparisons across landscapes”.

qs.why: The model needs assumptions about movement, and those are precisely the assumptions that photos cannot provide. So the numbers stand on premises not proven by the images.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options open with the same admission of limitation, so the sign does not mark the key. The tiger stripe option is also refuted by “permit individuals to be identified and counted with reasonable confidence”; the larger archive option is refuted by “those assumptions are precisely what the photographs cannot supply”; the premise option about patterns is refuted by “The model requires assumptions about movement”.

qs.why: Penulis nyebut penolakan itu “unexciting” lalu langsung bilang itulah seluruh disiplinnya. Yakin, tapi ditahan.
qs.whyOthersFail: The three distractors are all held back like the key and are all coherent with the thesis, so the only difference is the target and the degree. The resigned option is refuted by “they can refuse to characterize a detection rate as a population”, which imposes an obligation; the proud option because they will be noticed is refuted by two phrases, “cannot control that process” and “That refusal is unexciting”; the reprimand to the newspaper is misdirected, because the closing sentence speaks about the researcher's refusal.

qs.why: The text says at some point between the model and the summary, the estimate loses its interval and acquires an air of authority it never actually possessed.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options use the same two-way contrast and each distractor shifts exactly one element. The option about widened intervals reverses “loses its interval”; the option about being recalculated at the ministry adds a step not mentioned, as only translation into a summary is mentioned; the authority option gained from additional photos is refuted by “an air of authority it never possessed”.

qs.why: The text says animals that avoid paths are actually underrepresented, while those that frequently pass paths are overrepresented. The claim reverses that direction, so it is False.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” directly contradicts the camera placement sentence. “Not stated” is wrong because the direction of the bias is explicitly mentioned.

qs.why: The text says restoring acoustic devices only restores a portion, and the missing part is the listener. The equipment can be brought back, but the ears of the old audience cannot.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options use the “X can be restored, but Y cannot” form which is of equal precision. The intention option that can be restored is refuted by “intention is precisely what no instrument preserves”; the space option that can be restored reverses the list of what survives, “a manuscript, sometimes an instrument”; the first hearing option that can be restored reverses the key and is refuted by “the missing fraction is the listener”.

qs.why: The source is said to be largely teacher treatises complaining about students, and the text adds that complaints are only evidence of unusual practice. So the guide is only partial.
qs.whyOthersFail: The audience description option clashes with “consisted largely of treatises written by teachers”; the strong evidence option clashes with “The confidence was disproportionate to the evidence”; the practice considered normal reverses “only of unusual practice”.

qs.why: After a serious paragraph about arguments that age poorly, the short sentence about “sleeve notes” is intended to deflate the tone.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options mention the same amused tone, so what must be read is what the sentence does. The summary option is refuted by the sentence's own form, “Somebody should tell the sleeve notes”, which cuts rather than summarizes; the marketing direction warning option adds a prediction not made; the personal admission option adds an attitude of the author toward himself that is not in the text.

qs.why: The same sentence says scientific disputes about ornament acquired the vocabulary of a moral controversy. So the word accuses of destruction, rather than describing a different interpretation.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option about destroying instruments uses the literal meaning of “vandals”, even though the sentence pairs it with ornamental disputes that acquired “the vocabulary of a moral controversy”; the option about being considered old-fashioned weakens the accusation into a matter of taste; the option about negligence without malicious intent clashes with the word “vandals” itself.

qs.why: The text states that “historically informed” has replaced “authentic” on most covers. The claim simply summarizes this in other words, so it is True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” requires a statement that the term remained, which is not there. “Not stated” fails because the change of terms is mentioned directly.

qs.why: The pattern only appears if the notes are read in sequence, and anyone holding the pen on any given Tuesday could not see it. Thus, the meaning belongs to the series.
qs.whyOthersFail: One entry is ruled out because the text says “A single record proves little and doubts nothing”. Family piety is ruled out because the author explicitly rejects that term in the fourth paragraph. And institutions are ruled out because the grandfather never submitted a single observation, yet his notes are still called valuable.

qs.why: If you do not predict, you have nothing to defend. That is what leads the author to conclude his grandfather was protected from the desire to be vindicated by the weather.
qs.whyOthersFail: The author calls it a deliberate refusal, so it is not a result of a lack of training. Usefulness to researchers was never the intention; the aggregate itself was not the goal. And the notes were still written every morning for forty-one years, so it is not a sign of losing interest.

qs.why: What replaces the sensation of vindication is called “duller and more durable”, namely a mild curiosity about what the series will articulate. It is an exchange, not a loss.
qs.whyOthersFail: All four options name the same exchange, namely the sensation of vindication, so that word no longer marks the key and what distinguishes the content of the replacement. The option is still annoyed by being refuted by “I do not lament the sensation of vindication”; the option forced by the colleague's question is wrong because that question is only about what the notebook proves, while the shift “required several weeks to clarify itself”; the option that cannot be explained is refuted by the sentence that explicitly mentions the replacement, “a mild curiosity concerning what the series will eventually articulate”.

qs.why: The sentence says a single record proves little and doubts nothing, while a long record automatically doubts the year it happens to occupy.

qs.why: The text says the first frost comes later throughout the four decades. The claim just changes the word choice, so it is True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” requires the opposite direction, and that is not there. “Not stated” fails because the pattern is mentioned explicitly in that sentence.

qs.why: The text says the determinant is not a spirit of togetherness, but the shape of the movement path. This key reformulates that finding.

qs.why: Paragraph three mentions the cost: stair access consumes floor area that does not generate rent, and the closing sentence locks in the prediction that the stair “is usually deleted first”.
qs.whyOthersFail: The option of removing elevators clashes with the economic reasoning: the arrangement of elevators and corridors is actually cheaper for every party except the residents. The common room option is discarded after the maintenance dispute uses the effect as the cause, and the text mentions that dispute is one “no committee can settle”.

qs.why: The phrase “usually deleted first” is a bitter irony: the cheapest and most socially valuable thing is the first to be cut.

The option of accepting wearily is refuted by the proposed suggestion, “It recommends that circulation be treated as a social instrument rather than as a technical residue, and costed accordingly”; the option of blaming residents is off-target because “the studies compare structures, not residents”; the optimism option is refuted by “requires a vocabulary appraisals do not currently possess”.

qs.why: The text says the problem of honesty in this genre is not deception in each shot, but the systematic enlargement of events. That is the content of this key.

qs.why: That short sentence is striking: what we recognize first is the story pattern, not the animal. Its function is to dismantle the dominance of narrative conventions.
